title: feat(app,ui): fixture plates - parametric grid/dowel plates, fixtures placed at grid holes
body:
Stacked on #802

## What changed

CamCraft now has built-in, generic, parametric **fixture (grid) plates**, and any fixture can be placed **at a named grid location or on a dowel pair** of a plate, as one undoable command. It follows #802's pattern: generated watertight mesh, parameters on `FixtureDef`, insert/set commands over `InsertFixture`/`UpdateModel`, per-item drafts in a name-keyed map, and MCP tools. The code is in new files (`app::plate`, `plate/{grid,mount,detect,table}.rs`, `commands/fixture_plate.rs`, `mcp/plate_tools.rs`, `project/plate_dto.rs`, `ui` `state_plate.rs`, `fixture_plate_{dialog,rows,tests}.rs`, `plate_viz.rs`), with small hooks into shared files.

- **The plate (`app::plate`).**
  - Parameters: length, width and thickness; hole grid (pitch X/Y, first-hole offset); thread name and diameter; an optional dowel lattice (pitch, offset, diameter); optional counterbores.
  - The collision mesh is a **solid slab** (12 triangles, holes drawn solid), which is conservative. There is no new collision code: the plate is judged by the existing mesh laws.
  - Nonsense figures are refused by name: non-finite or non-positive values, a first hole over the edge, a thread as wide as the pitch, dowels running into tapped holes, a counterbore deeper than the plate, or more than 20000 holes.
- **Grid convention.** Rows are lettered along the plate frame's +Y from A (A..Z, AA, AB, ...), and columns are numbered along +X from 1. A1 is the hole nearest the frame's origin corner, so B3 is the second row's third hole. A built-in plate's frame has its origin at the plate corner on its **top** face, with the slab below z = 0. Dowel holes are a second lattice, named the same way.
- **Presets** (our own round figures; no vendor model or dimension):

  | Preset | Size | Thickness | Grid | Extras |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 12 x 12 in | 12 x 12 in | 0.75 in | 3/8-16 on 1 in, A1 at 0.5 in | |
  | 300 x 300 mm | 300 x 300 mm | 20 mm | M8 on 25 mm | 10 mm dowels on 50 mm, set between the tapped holes |
  | 400 x 300 mm | 400 x 300 mm | 30 mm | M12 on 50 mm | counterbored 18 x 12 mm |
  | 770MX table 28 x 15 in | sized from `tormach-770mx.mch`'s table box (its X/Y travel spans; a test pins it against the file) | 0.75 in | 3/8-16 on 1 in | |

  "Lay it on the machine table" centres a plate on the setup machine's table.
- **Placement (`PlaceOnPlate`).**
  - At a hole, the fixture's frame origin sits over the hole. On a dowel pair, it sits on the first dowel with +X toward the second.
  - The placement can be turned by a yaw. The fixture stands **on** the plate: its lowest point rests on the top face, so a vise's base sits on the plate whatever the model origin.
  - The location is recorded on the fixture's marker.
  - Refused by name: an unknown location, a gap, a dowel pair on a plate without dowels, a fixture hanging off the plate (the side and the amount are named), a fixture on itself or on a plate that rides on it, and a non-finite turn.
- **Moving the plate moves its fixtures.**
  - `MoveFixture` carries every fixture on a moved plate, transitively (a subplate carries its own), in the same single undo step.
  - `SetPlate` (editing a built-in plate) re-seats each fixture at its named location on the new grid.
  - Moving a placed fixture by hand takes it off its grid location, within that same undo step.
- **Grid from an imported plate (`SetPlateGrid::detect`), landed here rather than split off.**
  - It runs the Detect holes rule (`drilling::recognize`, the rule behind MCP `detect_holes`) on the model's own facets and groups the holes by diameter.
  - The largest group that forms an axis-aligned lattice becomes the grid; gaps are named. The next lattice group becomes the dowels.
  - A checkerboard pattern is read as a **staggered** grid: names come from the full lattice, and the off places are refused by name.
  - Holes off any pitch, or no Z holes at all, are refused by name.
- **Project file.** The fixture marker gets two optional keys, `plate` and `on_plate`, with no version bump. Following the #812 lesson, both are read leniently: a key that doesn't parse or breaks the plate law is dropped and logged, the fixture and its saved steel stay, and the load never fails.
- **MCP.** `add_fixture_plate`, `set_fixture_plate`, `place_on_plate`, `detect_plate_grid`, `get_plate_grid`. Each edit is one History step. The `camcraft-mcp` skill table is a process file, so I left it for the next process sync, as #802 did.
- **UI.**
  - "Add fixture plate…" on the Fixtures node menu and the Fixtures page (the fixture library's modal).
  - A plate's row shows its grid and what it carries.
  - Every fixture row gets **Place on plate…**: pick the plate, a row letter and column number (or a dowel pair) and a turn, then Place on grid.
  - Imported fixtures get **Detect plate grid**.
  - The viewport marks every hole, with dowels drawn differently, and labels row A and column 1.
- **Decisions:** `docs/decisions/819-fixture-plates.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `app fixture_plate` (7 tests):
  - `every_preset_builds_a_watertight_slab_of_its_exact_dimensions`
  - `grid_locations_are_letters_by_row_and_numbers_by_column`
  - `the_770mx_preset_is_its_machine_files_table_and_lies_on_it`
  - `a_vise_at_a_grid_location_lands_there_and_rides_the_plate`: H10 turned 90 degrees, the exact pose; moving the plate carries the vise in one undo; `SetPlate` re-seats it; a hand move unmounts it.
  - `bad_locations_overhangs_and_nonsense_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_plate_is_judged_by_the_posting_gate`: a face pass into the plate is convicted by `posting::verification_gate`, and one over it is clean.
  - `plates_and_places_survive_a_save_and_unreadable_keys_are_dropped`: the round trip, then unknown shapes in both keys load with the keys dropped and logged.
- `app fixture_plate_detect` (2 tests):
  - `an_imported_plates_grid_comes_from_its_holes`: a synthetic plate with a 5 x 7 grid, one gap and a 2 x 3 dowel lattice; fixtures snap to B2 and to a dowel pair; holes off the pitch and a plate with no holes are refused.
  - `a_staggered_plates_grid_is_read_as_staggered`
- `app mcp_plate`: `a_plate_is_added_a_vise_placed_on_its_grid_and_undone_over_mcp`.
- `ui` lib:
  - `fixture_plate_tests` (5 tests): the menu and page entry; the dialog places a plate with undo; a refusal is named in the dialog; a row places a vise at H10 with undo; Detect plate grid's refusal.
  - `tests::fixture_rows::a_fixture_plate_row_fits_the_default_pane` (structural).
- **A vendor plate STEP** was checked locally (never committed). Detection found its tapped holes as one size and read them as a staggered lattice on a regular pitch, with a few named gaps. Its odd-sized bores don't form a rectangular lattice, so they weren't taken as dowels. That file is why the staggered rule exists.

Gates:

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/788-builtin-vises`): app: the lib plus every gate-mapped suite (fixture_plate, fixture_plate_detect, mcp_plate, builtin_vise, fixtures, fixture_library, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, mcp, posting, ...) green in 202 s. ui: the lib (466 passed after updating the two Fixtures menu-label asserts in `fixture_library_tests` and `fixture_ux_tests`) plus 11 suites, green.
- Linux batch gate: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app suites and clippy -D warnings green; in the ui suites every target passed except `trace_parity`, which died with SIGSEGV (a headless-GPU crash under the parallel run; this PR doesn't touch the trace code). Re-run alone at the same head on the same box, it passed 3 of 3 (5 tests each).
- No snapshot PNG changed. The Fixtures page gains an "Add fixture plate…" button, and plates draw grid markers in the viewport. Neither appears in any golden without a plate, except the page button, which may move a release-lane golden of that page; those are regenerated at the cut.

## Not exercised

- I haven't checked the GUI by hand: the dialog in the running app, the plate and its markers in the viewport, or the picker's combos.
- The user's real plate on their 770MX: the 770 XL setup, with mod vises placed by hole.
- Dowel detection on a real plate whose dowel bores form a lattice. The vendor file's bores don't.
- A grid turned in its model frame is refused, not fitted.

Changelog: Fixture plates: parametric grid/dowel plates (12 x 12 in, 300/400 mm, 770MX table) in the fixture library, any fixture placed at a named grid hole or dowel pair in one undoable step and carried when the plate moves, and an imported plate's grid detected from its holes (#819)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #819

title: refactor(sim): the field column read from below - march_up, the mirrored sliver law, the shell-crossing read (#637 E2b)
body:
Stacked on #784 (on #782).

Part of #637 (step E2b, design in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637#issuecomment-6787218007 sections 2-3). Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed

- **`march_up` (new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/march_up.rs`)** - the mirror of `march`/`refine`: the same keyed probe and budgets, rising from the world floor, descending from the first material probe to the LOWEST material centre, and reading the floor from the `cut_downs` record there (a flipped bake's `cut_ups` records moved whole) or the shell's lowest crossing in the bracket, the higher binding.
- **`column_span` reads both sides.** The top is `march`'s; the floor is `march_up`'s whenever the field holds any `cut_downs`. A field with none keeps E1's monotone law (a material centre proves the shell floor) with no ascent, so the upright path is byte-identical in value and cost.
- **The shell-crossing read (both marches).** `refine` read an uncut surface at the cell boundary where the stored sign flipped - exact only for a lattice-aligned plane. Both `refine`s now read the cached parity column's crossing inside the bracket (`march::shell_in`), exact to rounding for any plane; where a cut entry and a crossing both bind, the one nearer the material centre wins (`march::face`, the column engine's own `min(top, cut)`). On aligned fixtures the crossing IS the boundary, so the parity and verdict suites read the same floats.
- **Neither a crossing nor a record is `Unreadable`.** On an upright field it cannot happen (every proven-inside cell records entry 0, and the cell under it a finite entry); it does for a flipped bounded tool's bottom face, which the old code would have guessed at the boundary. Refused by name instead.
- **The sliver law is one scan.** With no material centre the material lies between two adjacent air centres: the lower centre's `cut_ups` entry is the upper cut's bottom, the upper centre's `cut_downs` entry is the lower cut's top, the shell binds where no record does, a centre proven inside a cut is that cut's whole half-line. It reads E1's floor sliver, its mirror under a flipped cut, and a sliver floating between a cut from below and one from above. An air centre strictly inside the shell proves a cut, so a missing record there is refused, as E1 refused.
- **E2a's interim refusal lifted.** `turned` no longer sets `bounded_cuts` on a flipped bake; the flag follows the tool alone. Commit 1 pins the interim `CutFromBelow` on a flipped bake (the #784 review note); commit 2 replaces that pin with the exact read.
- **A level facet's crossing is exactly its height** (`solid_rest::plane_claim`, commit 3). The heavy lane caught the crossing read's one caveat: the barycentric sum rounds by an ulp on some rays even when the facet's three z are equal (the stepped facing golden's uncut columns at y = -6.25 read 2.0 + 1 ulp over a 2.0 stock top, and the rest ladder's strict `above(2.0)` mask disagreed where the old boundary read was exact by accident). A facet whose three z are equal now answers that z; a tilted facet keeps the sum. E1's floor on those columns reads -638.0 instead of -638.0000000000001 too. Pinned by `solid_rest::tests::a_level_facet_crosses_at_exactly_its_height` (three boxes, 441 rays each, bit for bit).
- `down_at` moves from a `cfg(test)` helper in `field_turn` to `field_ray` beside `up_at`. `floor_at` keeps its API. No column-engine verdict, golden or snapshot changes.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/780-field-march-up.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests (all in `crates/sim/tests/`):

- `field_floor`: `a_flipped_bake_reads_a_cut_floor_exactly_from_cut_downs` (the exact read where the interim refusal was pinned, plus the upright bake unchanged), `a_flipped_slot_through_the_plate_reads_empty_and_its_neighbours_exact`, `a_flipped_sliver_under_the_top_is_read_from_the_record_above_it` (0.2 sliver, the zero-height column, a hair past it empty), `a_flipped_bounded_tool_refuses_by_name` (`Unreadable` for the taper's unrecorded bottom face, `CutFromBelow` where its cut came near the new floor), `an_unaligned_plane_reads_its_shell_crossing_on_both_sides` (top 0.1 / floor -6.3 on a 0.5 cell, uncut and flipped with a slot).
- `carry_engine_agreement`: `a_baked_turn_reads_what_the_view_reads_through_every_turn` now compares the whole `column_body` read-back bit-for-bit through all 8 turns, flips included (the skip is gone); `an_unaligned_block_top_carries_the_same_on_both_engines` (top 5.1: slot, sliver, through); the cut-after-flip fixture (`cut_after_flip_agrees`: block, slot from the top, flipped through the bake with the translation applied to the moves by hand, slot from the new top across it, every column's top, floor, `empty_at` and the volume equal to the column body's to 1e-6): `a_slot_cut_after_the_flip_carries_the_same_on_both_engines` (3.0 / 4.0), `a_sliver_between_a_cut_from_below_and_one_from_above_carries_the_same` (3.0 / 2.2 and 2.7 / 2.6 - a sliver floating between the two cuts), `a_second_slot_through_the_first_carries_the_same_on_both_engines` (3.0 / 1.5 and -1.0 / 2.5).
- `field_turn` unit test: a flipped bake no longer sets `bounded_cuts`.

Agreement results: every column agrees to 1e-6 (tops, floors, `empty_at`, volume) through all 8 turns for the slot, deep slot, through-slot, floor sliver and unaligned-top fixtures; the off-grid ball slot within its 1e-3 march tolerance as before; the baked read-back is bit-identical to the view's for all 8 turns.

Locally (macOS, debug): `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` lib (68) and `field_floor`, `field_body`, `field_carry`, `carry_engine_agreement`, `stock_sdf`, `stock_sdf_cut`, `stock_backend_parity`, `field_arc_sweep`, `stock_field_cost`, `field_block_cost`, `stock_carry`, `stock_sim` - all green; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `hidden_rest_banded`, `ridge_rest` green; the touched sim suites' `--ignored` lanes in release green. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/779-field-turn-bake`: sim suites (27 binaries + lib), motion `posed_subtract`, app `stock_export` + `verify` - 0 failed (1.2 min wall, run twice: before and after commit 3). App's heavy lane `stock_engine_agreement` (release, `--ignored`): 3 passed - `both_engines_judge_every_golden_program_alike` over every golden program, the feed sampler and the Pocket3D consumers agree (this lane is what caught the level-facet ulp; it is green with the fix).

Linux batch gate: 0 failed - every tier step (geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion with its slow lanes, app with center_cut_multiaxis, ui, clippy -D warnings), 15.1 min wall.

## Not exercised

- `CarriedField::simulate` through the residual translation (E2c, #781) - the cut-after-flip fixture applies the translation to the moves by hand. The app holders (#586) and the default flip (#589) are untouched.
- Multi-crossing (undercut) meshes: the floor under a cut from below is the lowest material centre's cell crossing (the hull law), as the top has always been the highest's; no fixture has sub-cell slabs on both sides.
- Quarter turns with flips are covered by the 8-turn suite only on the block fixtures.

Changelog: none (internal: the field engine is not the default; no shipped verdict changes)
Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #780

title: fix(app): judge a table A with no axis vector; name pre-#804 machines on load
body:
Stacked on #810 (on #798)

Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed
Follow-ups to the #804 index-swing check, from the review of PR #810.

- **A table A with no axis vector is judged** (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs`). Before, a work-turning rotary whose `.mch` stated no `axis` vector wasn't judged at all, a silent pass. Now the clause reads the rotary's line from its `axis` vector, or with none, from its RS-274 letter:
  - **`A`:** about X, judged like the microARC's. The post writes a leaning tool axis as an A turn about X whatever the file says.
  - **`B` / `C`:** off X, outside this clause, as before.
  - **No vector and no RS-274 rotary letter** (say `U`): every op is refused by name, asking for the rotary's `axis`. Its line is unknown, so it could be an A under the tool.
- **Projects saved before #804 are named on load** (`crates/app/src/project/swing_note.rs`, `crates/post/src/machine/def.rs`). `AxisLimits::turns_part` is now `Option<bool>`. A parsed rotary always states it (`true` for a table, `false` for a head tilt), so a rotary read back with no `turns_part` key was saved before #804. Opening such a project adds a load note through the existing load-note path (also logged), e.g. `the document's machine Tormach 770MX + microARC 4 was saved before rotaries stated whether they turn the work: rotary A is not judged by the index-swing check - reload the machine so it is`. Only rotaries on, or possibly on, the X line are named. No project version step is needed: the key stays additive, and a fresh save writes it.
- **Tester kit README:** step 4 now says to keep the stored G30 Z at the top of travel, because the check assumes Z stays at the top while a `G30` turns A.
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the axis-vector rule. The decision record is `docs/decisions/813-swing-gaps.md`, covering what was chosen, what was dropped and why.

## How tested
New tests in `crates/app/tests/index_swing.rs` (9 now, up from 6):
- `a_custom_table_a_with_no_axis_vector_is_judged_about_x`: this is the shipped microARC text with the A's `axis` struck out.
  - A too-long tool is refused by name, the post errs and nothing is written.
  - A short tool clears.
- `a_work_turning_rotary_with_no_line_and_no_rs274_letter_is_refused_by_name`: the rotary is renamed `U` and has no vector. The post is refused by name and nothing is written.
- `a_project_saved_before_804_names_its_unjudged_table_a_on_load`:
  - A fresh save opens with no note.
  - The same save with `turns_part` stripped opens with one note, naming the machine and rotary A and asking for a reload.
  - A machine with no rotary gets no note.

The existing tests now assert `turns_part == Some(true)` for the microARC and `Some(false)` for the tilt-head's rotaries.

**Revert checks:**
- With the letter fallback removed (an unstated vector read as off X), the two axis tests fail and the other seven pass.
- With the note's `notes.extend` removed, the load test fails and the other eight pass.

Local results (macOS):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| index_swing | 9 passed |
| tormach_fourth_axis | 12 passed |
| microarc_test_part | 2 passed |
| machine | 33 passed |
| machine_library | 11 passed |
| project_roundtrip | 71 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| one_wcs | 8 passed |
| tilt | 8 passed |
| rotary_letter | 3 passed |
| rotary_verify | 9 passed |
| post_not_judged | 4 passed |
| camcraft-post (all) | passed |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The Linux quick gate (`--base upstream/main`) is running; I'll comment its result.

## Not exercised
- **UI:** the load note was not seen in the GUI. It rides the existing `open_noted` / `load_noted` path that the #342 notes use, and that path is tested headlessly.
- **A pre-#804 tilt-head project** gets the note too: the file can't tell a head tilt from a table A. Reloading clears it. This case isn't pinned by its own test.
- **Hardware:** nothing has been run on a machine.

Changelog: The A-index swing check also judges a work-turning A whose machine file states no axis vector (an A is about X), and refuses a work-turning rotary with neither a vector nor an A/B/C letter. A user's own table-A machine file that doesn't state `nose_to_axis` now has every operation refused by name until it does. Opening a project saved before the check names any embedded rotary it can't judge and asks for the machine to be reloaded.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #813

title: fix(sim,motion,app): plasma laws judge hole slugs and the reverse crossing; refuse a zero-width slit
body:
Stacked on #791

Branched from #791's head `40f256b4` (`issue/672-plasma-laws-2`); until #791 merges, this PR's diff also shows its commits - the new work is the single commit on top. Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed
Follow-ups from the three reviews of #791 (#672 step 2). Decisions in `docs/decisions/801-plasma-followups.md`.

1. **Tip-up over a freed hole slug** (`sim::verify::plasma`). A rapid is now judged against every earlier closed ring, not only OUTER ones; a hit on a hole is `TipUp { slug: true }`, read "crosses the slug of hole C<n>". No slug-size floor (whether a slug drops depends on the slat pitch, which the program does not know; the finding is a warning). The rapid leaving the hole just cut starts on its own slug (a hole's lead-out ends on the scrap side), so its first stretch is the departure and is not judged against that hole; a later stretch back over the slug is.
2. **The reverse inside-part crossing.** When the later cut is OUTER, an earlier ring with a stretch strictly inside it that it does not strictly enclose is a `CutCrossing` (L cut first, then E around it). INNER is left alone, so a nested part touching its hole's wall, cut first, stays common-line legal.
3. **Inch and G41/G42 at the gate** (`plasma_gate`). An inch document reads clean, and a cut crossing blocks the post with its place in inches (mm in a mm document). A control-compensated program is judged on its torch-centre moves (same rings as the computer-offset program) and the same cuts laid outline-first are refused.
4. **The vacuous diamond-hole pin** is replaced by a nested part touching its hole's wall, cut first, which reaches the laws (kerf warning only).
5. **Decision 4a** now states plainly that the 2r cap refuses a normal-sized inside V sharper than about 30 degrees; pinned by a 20 mm, 25-degree V refused.
6. **Zero-width slit.** `Region::new` keeps area, so an out-and-back spike in a picked contour vanished and the plate generated as the plain rectangle. `Region::new` is right for regions (milling asks for area) and is unchanged, so no geo2d issue is filed. The plasma contour door (`motion::plasma::nest::contours`) now refuses, by name and place, a picked vertex the normalised ring no longer reaches ("pick the slit as an open run"). A collinear vertex the region drops stays legal.

## How tested
Pins (each refusal removed and the pin seen to fail, then restored):

| Removed | Fails |
|---|---|
| slug tip-up (filter back to OUTER) | sim `plasma_laws::a_rapid_over_a_freed_hole_slug_is_a_tip_up_naming_the_hole`, `a_rapid_leaving_a_hole_and_running_back_over_its_slug_is_a_tip_up`; sim `plasma_program::a_rapid_over_a_freed_hole_slug_is_read_and_warned` |
| departure exemption | the two `plasma_laws` slug tests above |
| reverse crossing | `plasma_laws::a_part_cut_around_an_earlier_ring_running_through_it_is_refused` |
| slit refusal | motion `plasma::tests::a_zero_width_slit_in_a_picked_contour_is_refused_not_dropped` |
| document units in `posting_plasma::describe` | app `plasma_gate::an_inch_document_is_judged_the_same_and_placed_in_inches` |
| plasma refusals as gate problems | app `plasma_gate`: the two inch/G41-G42 pins plus the two existing refusal pins |

Also new: motion `plasma::tests::a_normal_sized_v_sharper_than_30_degrees_is_refused`; `plasma_laws::a_ring_inside_an_earlier_part_touching_its_edge_is_refused` now uses the reaching fixture.

Local: sim `plasma_laws` 21/21, `plasma_program` 6/6; motion `plasma::tests` 16/16; app `plasma_gate` 6/6, `plasma_profile` 7/7, `conformance` 6/6; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Linux quick gate (`--base upstream/main`) on 873c76b4: sim, motion and app suites green, 0 failed (3.4 min).

## Not exercised
- No real-table check of how slugs actually drop; the no-floor rule is a reasoned default (decision 1).
- The slit refusal is pinned on an axis-aligned spike; near-zero-width (not exact) slits still reach the cover law and its 2r cap as before.
- UI and MCP surfaces: no change (they read the same gate).
- `crates/sim/tests/plasma_laws.rs` is 404 lines (a test file just over the ~400 guideline).

Changelog: Plasma laws warn on a rapid over a freed hole slug, refuse an earlier ring running through a later part, and the plasma profile refuses a zero-width slit in a picked contour instead of dropping it.

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #801

title: feat(app,ui): built-in 5-axis self-centering vises, centred on the stock
body:
Stacked on #802

## What changed

CamCraft now has built-in 5-axis self-centering vises at 52, 75, 80 and 125 mm jaw width. Both jaws close on the centre, so the clamped width comes from the stock and the vise sits centred on it. They're built on #802's built-in vise as a **style**, not a new fixture kind, so placement, editing, undo, the project key, the vise row and the MCP tools are all reused.

- **Geometry (`app::vise::self_centering`).** One generated closed shell: a body block the full length under the floor, two jaw blocks `jaw_body_depth` deep up to jaw height, and an optional dovetail lip. The lip is a step `lip_depth` deep and `lip_height` above the jaw top, flush with the clamping face and drawn solid (the undercut is filled, so it never shows less steel than the real jaw). It's extruded across the overall width, so the jaws are drawn as wide as the body, as in #802. Repeated and collinear corners are dropped before ear clipping. A vise closed to 0 mm becomes one merged jaw block, and jaws at the body's ends run flush with it; both stay a single watertight shell.
- **Frame.** The origin is midway between the jaw faces at the floor, centred across the jaws, with the faces at y = ±opening/2. "Fit to the stock" centres the vise on the stock in X and Y, puts the floor under it and closes the jaws to its Y extent.
- **Refused by name:**
  - non-finite, zero or negative figures;
  - an opening outside the clamping range, or a min opening not below the max;
  - a non-zero screw housing (a self-centering vise has none);
  - a lip with only one of its two figures, or a lip deeper than the jaw body;
  - a body too short to carry both jaw bodies at the max opening;
  - stock wider or narrower than the clamping range, at Fit or at Open to stock;
  - stock off the vise's centre at Open to stock. Drawing the jaws at the far side would put the near jaw short of where the real jaw stops.
- **Commands.** These are #802's `InsertVise` / `SetVise`, one undo each. `ViseParams` gains `style: ViseStyle` (`Standard` or `SelfCentering { min_opening, lip_height, lip_depth }`). Only the law, the mesh, the fit and the opening-from-stock branch on it. `SetVise::from_stock` now asks the params (`ViseParams::opening_to_stock`), so each style measures its own way.
- **Project file.** An optional `self_centering` key inside the `vise` key, with no version bump. A build without it reads the zero housing as a broken standard vise and keeps the facets as plain steel (logged), never a wrongly regenerated vise.
- **MCP.**
  - `add_builtin_vise`: the four rows are in its `size` enum, and the description covers the centred frame.
  - `dimensions` (both tools): takes `min_opening`, `lip_height` and `lip_depth`, refused by name on a standard vise.
  - The vise view reports `style`.
  - No follow-up issue is needed.
- **UI.** The built-in vise dialog has a second size row, "5-axis self-centering". Picking one swaps the housing fields for **Min opening**, **Dovetail lip height** and **Dovetail lip depth**. The fit checkbox reads "centred, jaws closed on it", and the pose fields read **Centre X/Y**. The placed vise's row (Jaw opening, Set opening, Open to stock) is #802's, unchanged.
- **Tilted setups.** There's no new collision code. The vise is a meshed fixture, so the post gate's per-op law (`fixture_struck::op_hits`: box broad phase, then #339 slice 3's mesh refinement of the posed stack) judges it. It's pinned below.
- **Decisions:** `docs/decisions/787-self-centering-vises.md`.

Separate files where possible (`vise/self_centering.rs` and the new tests), so the #789 stack on the same base merges cleanly. The prism extrusion is duplicated locally (about 20 lines) rather than refactoring #802's `vise/mesh.rs`.

## Size table

Typical values in our own rounded, generic proportions; no vendor's model is copied. All figures are in mm. Jaw height is above the floor the part sits on; base height is the body, from table to floor. The dovetail lip is off by default. Sources are cited in the decision file: 5thaxis.com V5275 and V75100X, mate.com DynoGrip-52 80 mm, lang-technik.de Makro-Grip 125.

| Size | Jaw width | Jaw height | Jaw thick | Jaw body | Clamping | Length | Width | Base height |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 52 mm self-centering | 52 | 10 | 8 | 15 | 3.5-38.5 | 75 | 52 | 28 |
| 75 mm self-centering | 75 | 12 | 12 | 25 | 0-40 | 100 | 75 | 44 |
| 80 mm self-centering | 80 | 15 | 12 | 25 | 0-127 | 182 | 80 | 50 |
| 125 mm self-centering | 125 | 20 | 15 | 25 | 0-208 | 260 | 125 | 69 |

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `app self_centering_vise` (5 tests):
  - `every_self_centering_row_builds_a_closed_shell_of_its_dimensions`: all four rows at min, mid and max opening, each with no lip, a half-depth lip and a full-depth lip, plus jaws flush with the body's ends. Checks every directed edge has its reverse, the exact outward volume, centred bounds, that `FixtureMesh::build` accepts the mesh, that both jaws are solid and that the gap is open.
  - `the_table_keeps_the_issues_starting_figures`
  - `nonsense_parameters_are_refused_by_name`: 14 law refusals, plus stock wider and narrower than the range at placement.
  - `a_fitted_vise_is_centred_on_the_stock_and_closes_on_it`: off-origin stock. Checks the pose at the stock centre, steel just outside both stock sides and air just inside, re-closing when the stock grows, and the off-centre and too-wide refusals.
  - `placing_and_editing_are_one_undo_each_and_survive_a_save`: a lipped edit round-trips through save/load, and the reloaded vise keeps its own clamping-range law. Undo restores the exact facets, and redo works.
- `app self_centering_vise_tilted` (3 tests). Setup: 80 mm vise clamping 40 x 30 x 30 stock, 4 mm end mill, through `fixture_struck::op_hits`, the gate's per-op law.
  - `a_tool_leaning_into_a_jaw_strikes_it_where_upright_it_clears`. Tip 2 mm above the floor beside the stock, 10 mm off centre. **Upright:** clear, 3 mm off the jaw face. **Leaning 30 deg toward the jaw:** `FixtureHit` (the flute crosses the face about 6.5 mm up the axis, inside the 15 mm jaw). **Leaning away:** clear.
  - `the_same_lean_from_the_vise_centre_clears_the_jaws`: the same 30 deg lean from y 0 is clear. The vise's box alone covers the move, so the mesh is what acquits it.
  - `a_tilted_face_over_the_clamped_stock_posts_and_raised_jaws_block_it`: a 3+2 face indexed B 10 deg (every move posed) passes `posting::verification_gate`. With `SetVise` raising the jaws to 28 mm, the gate names the strike; undo clears it.
- `app mcp_self_centering_vise`: `a_self_centering_vise_is_fitted_edited_and_undone_over_mcp` covers the size enum, the fit centred at the origin, refusals (range, lip, housing, a standard vise's `min_opening`), lip and range edits, from_stock, and five undos.
- `ui` lib, `fixture_self_centering_tests` (4 tests, CWD `crates/ui`), structural only (AccessKit labels):
  - the dialog lists the sizes, and their own fields swap in;
  - Place fits the vise centred, and one undo removes it;
  - the clamping-range refusal is named in the dialog;
  - the row's Set opening and Open to stock work, with undo.
- #802's suites are unchanged and still pass: `builtin_vise` 9, `mcp_vise` 1, `fixture_vise_tests`, `tests::fixture_rows`.

Gates:

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/788-builtin-vises`): green. App lib plus 56 suites (59 s) and ui lib plus 3 suites (18 s): 1044 passed, 0 failed.
- Linux batch gate: green at 25db3c53 (geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui suites and clippy -D warnings; 9 steps, 0 failed, 15.1 min).
- No snapshot PNGs or process files changed.

## Not exercised

- I haven't checked the GUI by hand: opening the dialog in the running app, picking a self-centering size, placing it, seeing it drawn in the viewport, and editing the lip fields.
- No real rotary machine file. The tilted pins use posed tool axes (5-axis lean and a 3+2 index) against steel that turns with the part, which is the default. Steel marked "fixed" under a stated rotary axis is judged by the machine-frame law from #339 slice 3, unchanged here.
- The dovetail angle isn't modelled: the lip is a solid step at the face (see the decision file).

Changelog: Built-in 5-axis self-centering vises (52, 75, 80, 125 mm) in the fixture library: centred on the stock with the jaws closed on it, clamping range and dovetail lip editable, judged by the fixture mesh laws in upright and tilted setups (#787)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #787

title: feat(app): refuse an A index whose retracted tool can't clear the swept work
body:
Stacked on #798

Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed
Before every `G0 A..`, the PathPilot post lifts Z to the top of travel (`G53 G0 Z0`), and a `G30` can move A too. Until now nothing checked that the tool there clears what turns under it. The program gate now does.

- **New gate clause** (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs`, wired into `verification_report`). It checks every op whose machine has a rotary about X that turns the work.
  - **Tip height:** the tool tip sits at `nose_to_axis - tool length`, where tool length is cutter + shank + holder, with a modelled body counted.
  - **Swept radius:** the farthest vertex from the A line (through WCS Y0 Z0, along X) of the setup's stock, the parts, and the tagged fixtures that turn with the work. Fixed fixtures are left out.
  - **Refusal:** if the clearance is under 5 mm, the post is refused naming the op, the A, the tip height, the swept radius and the clearance, e.g. `FLAT: the A90.000 index turns the work under the tool - at the safe Z the tip of EM 1/4 (...) is ... mm above the A centerline, the stock, part and turning fixtures sweep 13.470 mm, a clearance of 3.000 mm against the 5.0 mm needed`.
- **Machine file statement `nose_to_axis`** (`crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs`, `def.rs`, `parse.rs`). This is the spindle nose's height above the rotary's centerline with Z at `safe_retract`.
  - A rotary turns the work (`AxisLimits::turns_part`) when no `head` part hangs below it. A head tilt, such as `tilthead.mch`, is unaffected.
  - A garbled value, or the key on any other part, refuses the file by name.
  - If a work-turning A about X states no `nose_to_axis`, every op is refused by name. The gate has no way to show the turn clears, so it refuses rather than warns.
- **`tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`** states `nose_to_axis: 10.6` in. That is Tormach's 770MX 13.75 in spindle nose to table, less the microARC 4's 3.15 in table to centerline (4th-axis comparison sheet 02/24).
- **Tester kit:** the `.camproj` is re-saved so its embedded machine carries the new facts. The kit `.nc` is byte-identical. README step 3 now says what the gate checks and what is still the operator's job (the chuck and jaws are unmodelled, and the figure comes from the spec sheet).
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key. The decision record is `docs/decisions/804-a-swept-radius.md`.

## How tested
New `crates/app/tests/index_swing.rs` (6 tests):
- `the_shipped_microarc_states_its_nose_height_and_a_work_turning_a`: also checks that the tilt-head's A turns the tool.
- `a_short_tool_over_the_kit_bar_clears_and_posts`: the kit's 3/4" bar with a 3" tool posts, `G0 A90` included.
- `a_tool_too_long_to_clear_the_bar_is_refused_by_name`: the clearance is 3 mm against 5. Refused by name, nothing written.
- `a_fat_chuck_turning_with_the_bar_is_refused_by_name`: a 400 mm turning fixture behind the bar.
- `a_work_turning_a_with_no_nose_height_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_machine_with_no_a_is_unaffected`: the same too-long tool on the plain 770MX.

Unit tests in `crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs` cover head vs table rotaries and the parse/refusal of `nose_to_axis`.

**Revert check:** with the clause removed from `verification_report`, the three refusal tests fail and the other three pass.

Local results:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| index_swing | 6 passed |
| tormach_fourth_axis | 12 passed |
| microarc_test_part | 2 passed (kit `.nc` unchanged) |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| tilt | 8 passed |
| machine | 33 passed |
| machine_library | 11 passed |
| machine_edit | 9 passed |
| project_roundtrip | 71 passed |
| rotary_letter | 3 passed |
| rotary_verify | 4 passed |
| post_not_judged | 12 passed |
| tormach_post | 10 passed |
| tormach_safe_retract | 4 passed |
| camcraft-post (all) | passed |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The Linux quick gate (`--base upstream/main`) is running; I'll comment its result.

## Not exercised
- **Hardware.** Nothing has been run on a 770MX with a microARC 4. The 10.6 in is the spec sheets' nominal figure, not a measurement, and the README still asks the operator to check at the top of Z.
- **Unmodelled chuck and jaws** are not judged.
- **Old projects:** a machine embedded in a project saved before this change has no `turns_part`, so it reads as not judged. Reloading the machine fixes it. The only shipped work-turning A is the new microARC file.
- **Machines pane:** it doesn't expose `nose_to_axis` as a field yet. The key is set in the `.mch` text.

Changelog: The program gate refuses an A index on a work-turning 4th axis (microARC 4) when the retracted tool tip can't clear the swept stock, part and turning fixtures by 5 mm; machine files state the new `nose_to_axis`.

**Changelog note (#813):** this PR also changes behaviour for custom machines. A user's own `.mch` with a table A about X that doesn't state `nose_to_axis` now has every op on that machine refused by name. The cut's changelog row should say so; the wording is in #815's `Changelog:` line.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #804

title: feat(app,ui): built-in workholding accessories in the fixture library
body:
Stacked on #802

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch base built before the sync; it carries #802 at c2a3f873).

## What changed

CamCraft now has built-in, generic workholding accessories beside #802's vises: parallels, 1-2-3 blocks, step blocks, strap (toe) clamps and soft jaws. Each is generated from a few dimensions and placed like any fixture, so the existing fixture laws judge it. There's no new collision code.

- **Geometry (`app::accessory`).** Each kind is one or more closed, outward shells that touch but never overlap, so the mesh law's ray-parity inside test holds. A strap clamp's stud is drawn below the strap and above it, not through it. Holes and slots are drawn solid, and the stud is a 16-sided polygon whose flats touch its diameter, so the shells never hold less steel than the real part. Nonsense is refused by name, naming the accessory and the dimension: a non-finite, zero, negative or over-5 m dimension, a step count outside 1-50, a stud past the toe or into the heel block, or a heel block as long as the strap.
- **Placement (`commands::InsertAccessory`).** This wraps `InsertFixture`, so the accessory lands as an ordinary model wearing `FixtureDef`, with its parameters on the marker (`FixtureDef::accessory`). You place it by pose. Parallels can instead be fitted **under the stock in a built-in vise**: the height is set so the stock's top stands a stated amount over the jaws, the pair stands on the vise floor against both jaws, and the vise drops to suit (a `MoveFixture`). All of that is one undo unit. It's refused by name if the stock already stands that high, or if two parallels don't fit in the opening.
- **Editing (`commands::SetAccessory`).** A resize regenerates the mesh through `UpdateModel` and swaps the marker, in one undo step. A resize keeps the kind. Re-binding keeps the parameters, and a re-import drops them, as for a vise.
- **Soft jaws** are a standalone block (width, height, thickness) placed at a jaw face, not a vise option. #802's review reshaped the vise's jaw profile (`jaw_body_depth`), and a soft-jaw option would have to reshape it again while #802 is still open. The reasoning is in the decision file.
- **Project file.** The fixture marker gets an optional `accessory` key, tagged by `kind`, with no version bump. An older build ignores it and keeps the facets. On load, a key that breaks the law is dropped and logged, and the fixture stays as plain steel.
- **UI.**
  - "Add accessory…" on the Fixtures node's menu and the Fixtures page, sharing the fixture library's modal. You pick a kind, edit its figures, then type a pose or, for parallels, pick a vise and set "Stock top over the jaws".
  - Each placed accessory's row shows its figures and "Apply sizes" (one `SetAccessory`). The drafts are kept per row in a map, following #802's per-vise opening drafts, so two rows never reset each other.
- **MCP.**
  - `add_accessory`: kind, setup, position/rotation or `under_stock_in_vise` + `above`, `steps`, and dimension overrides.
  - `set_accessory`: dimension overrides and `steps`.
  - Each call is one History step. No follow-up issue is needed. The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table is a process file, so I left it alone; it can list the tools in the next process sync.
- **Decisions:** `docs/decisions/789-workholding-accessories.md`.

## Defaults

These are our own generic figures in common inch sizes; no vendor model is copied. The code stores millimetres.

| Item | Defaults |
|---|---|
| Parallels (a pair) | height 1 in, thickness 1/8 in, length 6 in, spacing 4 in (gap between inner faces) |
| 1-2-3 block | 3 x 2 x 1 in, holes drawn solid |
| Step block | 6 steps, rise 1/2 in, run 3/4 in, width 1 in |
| Strap clamp | strap 6 x 1 1/4 x 5/8 in; stud 1/2 in, standing 1 1/2 in above the strap (nut and washer included), 2 1/4 in from the toe; heel block 1 1/4 in long; clamp height 1 in |
| Soft jaw | width 6 in, height 2 in, thickness 3/4 in |
| Parallels fit | stock top 1/4 in over the jaws |

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `app builtin_accessory` (3 tests):
  - `every_kind_builds_closed_shells_of_its_dimensions`: every kind, plus step blocks of 1-8 steps and a stud wider than the strap. Checks the mesh law's 2-cycle closure, the exact outward volume, the bounds, and that `FixtureMesh::build` accepts the mesh. The 1-2-3 block measures 1 x 2 x 3 in.
  - `nonsense_parameters_are_refused_by_name`
  - `placing_and_resizing_are_one_undo_each_and_survive_a_save`: placement and resize are each one undo, the revision moves, undo restores the facets, redo works, every kind's parameters survive a save/load and stay editable, and a hand-edited nonsense key loads as plain steel. A kind change and an imported fixture are refused.
- `app accessory_collisions` (2 tests):
  - `a_strap_clamp_stud_strikes_a_low_link_and_the_routed_link_clears_it`: the clamp is judged by its mesh. A link at z 50 across the stud is struck by the post gate's per-op law (`fixture_struck::op_hits`). The link #489 would lay (up, across at the clamp box top + 5 mm, down) is clear. The same z 50 over the strap beside the stud is clear too.
  - `parallels_fitted_under_the_stock_lift_it_over_the_jaws`: the face pass the 6 in vise's jaws struck posts clean once the parallels are fitted. Checks the height, spacing and positions, that one undo restores the vise, and the named refusals.
- `app mcp_accessory`: `accessories_are_placed_fitted_resized_and_undone_over_mcp`.
- `ui` lib:
  - `fixture_accessory_tests` (5 tests): the menu and page entry, a strap clamp placed from the dialog plus undo, parallels fitted from the dialog into the setup's vise, a refusal named in the dialog, and two rows keeping their own size drafts with Apply landing `SetAccessory` plus undo.
  - `tests::fixture_rows::a_built_in_accessory_row_fits_the_default_pane` (structural).
- Updated menu-label asserts in `fixture_library_tests` and `fixture_ux_tests`.
- Mutation check: with the stud's upper shell dropped from the strap clamp mesh, the strap clamp test fails.

Gates:

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/788-builtin-vises`): green, app (lib + every gate-mapped suite, including the three new ones) 197 s, ui lib + 11 suites 32 s, 0 failed.
- Linux batch gate: running; its result will be added as a PR comment.
- No snapshot PNG changed. The new "Add accessory…" button on the Fixtures page may move a release-lane golden that shows that page; those are regenerated at the cut.

## Not exercised

- I haven't checked the GUI by hand: opening the dialog in the running app, placing each accessory and seeing it drawn in the viewport, fitting parallels into a vise, and editing a row's sizes.
- #489's automatic routing over a clamp: #489 isn't on main, so the pin judges the link #489 would lay with the very law #489 consults, not the router itself. Once both are on main, a router-driven pin can be added to `fixture_route`.
- Accessories on rotary or tilted setups.

Changelog: Built-in workholding accessories in the fixture library (parallels with a fit under the stock in a built-in vise, 1-2-3 and step blocks, strap clamps, soft jaws): placed and resized in one undoable step each, judged by the fixture mesh laws (#789)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #789

title: feat(machine): refuse rigid tapping by name at the program gate; validate spindle.rigid_tapping
body:
## What changed

- **Program gate, every post.** The machine check (`machine::check_ops`, which every post path runs through `verification_report`) now refuses a path carrying tap cycles on a machine whose `.mch` states `spindle.rigid_tapping: false`. The message names the op, the cycle count and the machine: `Tap1: 1 tap cycle(s) need rigid tapping, which Tormach 770M cannot do - use a tapping head or thread milling`. Before this, only `tormach.cps` read `machine.rigidTapping`, so a 770M posted through Fanuc or Haas wrote a G84 with no warning. The cycle is never converted to another cycle. `tormach.cps` is unchanged and keeps its own refusal for the standalone script path. The gate is `judge::tap_gate` (`crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs`).
- **Schema validated.** A `rigid_tapping` value that isn't `true`, `false` or `null` now refuses the file by name, at the reader (`parse_mch`: `spindle.rigid_tapping must be true or false, not "no"`) and in the Machines pane's validator (key `spindle.rigid_tapping`). Before, `"no"` read as unstated, which means "not limited".
- **Machines pane.** The Spindle group's "Rigid tapping" row now reads `yes`, `no - tap cycles are refused`, or `not stated - not limited`, instead of the raw `true`/`false`. The structural UI test was updated; no snapshot PNG changed.
- **Machine files.** No `.mch` changed. Every Tormach mill and router already stated the value (#170, #618, #620): `true` on the four MX mills, `false` on the R8 M/M+ mills, the PCNC series and the routers. A new test pins the whole set. The lathes are unstated, so behaviour there is unchanged, and #795 tracks them.
- **Docs.** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` and `docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md` describe the key. The decision is in `docs/decisions/786-rigid-tapping.md`: explicit on the Tormach files, absent means "not limited". Default-false was considered and dropped because it would change every non-Tormach machine.

## How tested

Pinning tests (new `crates/app/tests/rigid_tapping.rs`):
- `a_tap_on_a_machine_that_cannot_rigid_tap_is_refused_by_name_whatever_the_post`: a tap job on the 770M through Tormach PathPilot, Fanuc and Haas, run through `posting::post_setup`. It is refused by name, no file is written, and the machine check names it. Fails with the gate line commented out (checked).
- `a_tap_posts_where_rigid_tapping_is_stated_or_unstated`: the 1100MX on PathPilot and the generic VMC on Fanuc still post G84, and the check stays silent.
- `rigid_tapping_must_be_a_boolean_or_the_file_is_refused_by_name`: both doors.
- `the_machines_sheet_states_rigid_tapping_in_words`
- `every_tormach_mill_and_router_file_states_rigid_tapping`
- UI: `egui_app::tests::machines_pane::the_sheet_states_rigid_tapping_in_words` (AccessKit labels).

Suites run on the final head (merged with v0.17.0), all green:
- camcraft-app: rigid_tapping 5, machine 33, machine_library 11, machine_edit 12, posting 17, conformance 6, golden_cl 24, tormach_machines 6, tormach_post 10, tormach_routers 5, plasma_machine 6, carvera_machines 1. Earlier head, also green: fanuc_post 11, solid_law_goldens 1, heidenhain_block_form 4.
- camcraft-post: all suites.
- camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` + `structural`: 11.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The 770MX G84 golden and every other golden are byte-identical; no golden file is in the diff.

## Not exercised

- The full quick gate (the coordinator runs it) and the batch and release tiers.
- A hand check of the Machines pane: the Rigid tapping row wording on a real window.

body:
Stacked on #800 (#793). This branch is cut from `issue/793-taper-holders`. Merge #800 first, then retarget this PR to `main`. Until then the diff below includes #800's commit.

## What changed

- **Standalone ER collet chucks (#792).** Six new library entries, "ER11 chuck" to "ER40 chuck". Each is drawn as its nut, then a body at the nut's diameter, up to the body's back face. That back face is the gauge line, where the straight shank enters the spindle or adapter. Default gauge lengths (nose face to back face) are 30 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 55 / 65 mm: typical chuck heads, rounded up.
- **BT40 ER40** is added, which #793 deferred to this issue. Its Ø63 nut is flush with the BT40 flange.
- **One ER table (#800 review).** `holder_library::ER_SIZES` (ER11-ER40) is the only ER nut table. The BT/CAT ER entries and the standalone chucks both draw from it.

| Size | Collet Ø | Thread | Nut Ø × length (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ER11 | 0.5-7 | M14×0.75 | 22 × 11.5 |
| ER16 | 0.5-10 | M22×1.5 | 32 × 17.5 |
| ER20 | 1-13 | M25×1.5 | 35 × 19.5 |
| ER25 | 1-16 | M32×1.5 | 42 × 20 |
| ER32 | 2-20 | M40×1.5 | 50 × 22.5 |
| ER40 | 3-26 | M50×1.5 | 63 × 29 |

The ranges and threads are from ISO 15488 / DIN 6499. The nut sizes are typical round-nut catalog values, not fixed by the standard: ER11 at the top of its makers' Ø19-22 range, and ER40 at its longest common length. Sources are in `docs/decisions/792-er-collets.md`.

### #800 review fixes (notes 1-3 and 5 as the brief numbers them)

- **Flare envelope.** A 45° cone runs from the body or nut radius out to the flange radius. It ends at the flange's front face and starts `(flange r - body r)` below it. The minimum gauge length grows to hold it. The bands read a sloped segment at its larger radius, so the judging laws see the flange reaching down to the cone's foot, which is more conservative still.
- **Weldon clamp screw.** A Weldon body is drawn 1.0 mm larger in radius (`WELDON_SCREW`) than its catalog diameter. This is an engineering allowance for a screw head standing proud; no public standard gives that figure. It replaces #793's "about flush, not drawn".
- **Projection in the picker.** A "projection" field (nose face above the tool tip) sits beside the gauge length. It starts at the stored tool's stickout and lands through the same `CommandKind::SetToolHolder` / `SetToolBody::library` (one undo step).
- **Optional review note 4.** The picker's live shank check now reads the stored tool, the same tool Apply judges.

### #800 numbers that moved

- The BT30 ER20 outline's body point moves from (90, 17.5) to (84.5, 17.5). That is the flare foot, 23 - 17.5 = 5.5 mm under the flange front.
- `a_longer_gauge_raises_the_flange_and_keeps_the_nose`: the first flange-width band is now 9.5 mm lower. That is the flare of BT40 Weldon 12 mm, body r 21 + 1 against flange r 31.5.
- The Weldon "Ø25 body" comment now notes it is judged at Ø27. All of #800's tests still pass.

### BT30 ER20 at the default 60 mm gauge, nose 52 mm above the tip (the user's setup)

| Point | Position |
|---|---|
| Nut | Ø35, 52-71.5 |
| Body | Ø35 to 84.5 |
| Flare | 45° to Ø46 at 90 |
| Flange | Ø46, 90-110 |
| Standoff | to the gauge line at 112 |

The standalone "ER20 chuck" (gauge 45) is: nut Ø35 × 19.5, then body Ø35 to the back face.

## How tested

- `camcraft-tools` lib, `holder_library::tests` (8 tests):
  - new: `the_er20_chuck_outline_is_the_table` (ER20, ER11 and ER40 chucks, point by point)
  - new: `the_flare_envelope_runs_45_degrees_into_the_flange_front` (every taper entry, and the min gauge refusal)

  - `a_weldon_body_strikes_within_its_clamp_screw_allowance`: a wall at 13 mm is struck, one at 14 mm is clear.
  - `an_er32_nut_strikes_a_wall_a_shank_cylinder_misses`: #792's acceptance. A Ø6 holder cylinder misses the wall the ER32 nut strikes, and a wall at 26 mm is clear.

title: fix(app): machine check reads a 4th-axis table's pose through the tool axis
body:
**Stacked on #798** (Tormach microARC 4, issue #785). This branch merges #798's head (`f99f045e`). Until #798 merges, this PR's diff also shows #798's files. Review only the files listed under "What changed". Merge #798 first, then re-check this PR with `git merge origin/main`.

Fork synced at v0.16.0 (process files PROCESS_VERSION 10). Upstream main is merged into this branch because the code it fixes landed after v0.16.0 (#785). Correction: #785's code has not landed on upstream main. It is still open as #798, which is why this PR is stacked on it.

## What changed

The machine check judged a tilted move's canonical letters one by one. On the 770MX + microARC 4, whose only rotary is an A about X, it refused the face underneath (A0 B180) with "states no B axis". That table reaches the pose as A180, and the PathPilot post already posts it as `G0 A180`.

- `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs`: the pose gate moves here from `mod.rs` as `pose_problems`.
  - On a machine with exactly one rotary, stated along X (the post's own test, x² ≥ 0.998·|d|²), the gate reads the tool angle about X from the letters. It uses the post's formula and tolerances (`tormach.cps` `toolAngle`), so the check and the post agree on every pose.
  - The angle is signed by the stated direction (a `[-1,0,0]` table commands the negated angle, as the post writes the word) and judged against the rotary's travel.
  - A pose with an X component, meaning any B or C a turn about X cannot make, is refused by name: `move i commands A .. B .. C .. deg; <model>'s only rotary, A about X, cannot reach that pose`.
  - Every other machine keeps the letter law unchanged: none, two or more rotaries, or a single rotary that is unstated or not along X.
- `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`: calls `pose_problems` instead of the inline letter loop. The file shrinks from 396 to 355 lines.
- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`: this post writes the stream's letters as they come (G43.4), so it now refuses a turning letter with no rotary of that name: `tilted move commands B - the machine states no B rotary`. Before this PR, the check stopped A0 B180 reaching that dialect on an A-only table. Now the post does, so the safety floor is unchanged.
- `crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs` (from #798): the wrap test now expects the post's refusal (`simultaneous 4-axis motion in operation WRAP`). It also asserts that the machine check no longer flags the wrap, whose every pose is reachable as an angle about X. The header comment is updated.
- `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/README.md`: one sentence updated to match.
- `docs/decisions/797-a-only-pose.md`: the decision record.

## How tested

The new suite, `crates/app/tests/fourth_axis_pose.rs`, holds the pinning tests:

- `an_a0_b180_slot_posts_as_a180_on_the_microarc4`: a real Slot with tilt A0 B180 on the bar job, built through the app's commands.
  - The check is clean.
  - `post_setup` writes exactly one index, `G0 A180`, and no B word.
  - The cuts land on the skin (Z 0.375 → 0.36) inside the stick-out.
- `the_face_underneath_is_judged_as_a180_against_the_travel`:
  - With A travel -90..90, every move is refused as `commands A 180.000 deg (the pose A 0.000 B 180.000), the travel is -90.000..90.000`.
  - A `[-1,0,0]` table commands -180: it passes on -180..0 and is refused on 0..180.
- `a_pose_the_a_axis_cannot_reach_is_still_refused_by_name`: a B30 lean on the same machine is refused by name by the check, and `post_setup` refuses and writes no file.
- `a_second_rotary_keeps_the_letter_law`: A about X plus C about Z still refuses B180 with `states no B axis`.
- `the_fanuc_dialect_refuses_a_b_on_an_a_only_table`: fanuc.cps on the microARC mirror refuses A0 B180 by name and writes no `B180`. A90 posts.

Gate: the plan from `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`. It falls to every app suite because #798's golden is shared test input. It was run with `-j 2` (the xtask hard-codes `-j 6`, which exhausts the Windows paging file here). Results per step:

- post suites (`camcraft-post --lib`): 7 passed.
- app suites (the lib plus 234 test binaries, `fourth_axis_pose` among them): 1775 passed, 1 failed. The one failure is `microarc_test_part::the_microarc_test_part_posts_its_indexed_program`. It comes from #798 and is a Windows checkout issue:

title: feat(app,ui): built-in parametric milling vises in the fixture library
body:
## What changed

CamCraft now has built-in, generic, parametric milling vises. They're placed like any fixture and judged by the existing fixture laws, with no new collision code.

- **Geometry (`app::vise`).** Each vise is built from ten parameters plus its jaw opening, as one closed shell with outward normals. The shell is the vise's side profile (base, fixed jaw, moving jaw at the opening, and a block for the screw and handle housing), extruded across the body width. The jaws are drawn as wide as the body, which errs on the safe side. The end caps are triangulated by ear clipping, so the mesh is watertight by construction. Bad parameters are refused by name: non-finite, zero or negative values, an opening over the max, a body narrower than the jaws, or a body too short to carry both jaws plus the housing.
- **Placement (`commands::InsertVise`).** This wraps the fixture library's `InsertFixture`, so a vise lands as an ordinary model wearing `FixtureDef`. Its parameters ride the marker (`FixtureDef::vise`), so delete/undo and re-binding to another setup keep them. Re-importing a file over a vise drops them. There are two ways to place one:
  - fit it to the setup's stock (fixed jaw on the stock's +Y side, centred in X, floor under the stock, jaws opened to the stock's Y width);
  - give a pose (the frame origin is the fixed jaw's clamping face, centred, at the floor).
- **Editing (`commands::SetVise`).** It changes the jaw opening or any dimension in one undo step. The mesh is regenerated through `UpdateModel` and the revision moves. "Open to stock" re-opens the jaws to the stock as the vise stands, measured along the vise's own screw axis. It's refused by name if the stock reaches into the fixed jaw or is wider than the max opening.
- **Project file.** The fixture marker gets an optional `vise` key, and the project version is not bumped. It's absent on imported fixtures. An older build ignores the key and keeps the saved facets. A vise key with invalid values is dropped and logged on load, and the fixture stays as plain steel.
- **UI.**
  - "Add built-in vise…" on the setup's Fixtures node menu and on the Fixtures page. The dialog shares the fixture library's modal: pick a size, edit any value, then Fit to the stock (the default) or type a pose.
  - A placed vise's row shows **Jaw opening**, **Set opening** and **Open to stock**. Each one queues `SetVise`.
- **MCP.**
  - `add_builtin_vise`: size, setup, `fit_to_stock` or position/rotation/opening, and dimension overrides.
  - `set_vise`: opening or `from_stock`, plus dimension overrides.
  - Each call is one History step. No follow-up issue is needed. The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table is a process file, so I left it alone; it can list the two tools in the next process sync.
- **Decisions:** `docs/decisions/788-builtin-vises.md`.

These are typical values in our own rounded, generic proportions; no vendor's model is copied. Sources are cited in the decision file. The code stores millimetres, converting inches at 25.4 mm.

| 8 in | 8 in | 2 in | 1 3/4 in | 8 1/4 in | 20 in | 9.5 in | 3.25 in | 2.5 x 1.5 in |
| 100 mm | 100 | 32 | 25 | 110 | 300 | 125 | 55 | 35 x 20 |
| 125 mm | 125 | 40 | 30 | 160 | 360 | 150 | 65 | 40 x 25 |
| 150 mm | 150 | 45 | 35 | 200 | 420 | 180 | 70 | 45 x 30 |
| 160 mm | 160 | 50 | 38 | 220 | 450 | 190 | 75 | 50 x 30 |

title: feat(tools,ui): built-in BT30/BT40/CAT40 holder library (ER and Weldon)
body:
## What changed

- **`camcraft-tools::holder_library`** (new). A built-in library of steep-taper holders, drawn as spun profiles (#93). There are 36 entries, each a taper (BT30, BT40 or CAT40) with an ER collet chuck or a Weldon side-lock nose:
  - **BT30:** ER16, ER20, ER25 and ER32; Weldon 6/8/10/12/16 mm and 1/4, 3/8, 1/2 in.
  - **BT40:** ER16, ER20, ER25 and ER32; Weldon 6-20 mm and 1/4-3/4 in.
  - **CAT40:** ER32; Weldon 1/4-3/4 in and 6-20 mm.

  `HolderEntry::points(nose, gauge_len)` draws the outline tip-up: the nut (or Weldon body), the body to the flange, the flange as a full cylinder, the standoff to the gauge line, then closed at the gauge line. A gauge length that is too short, a non-finite number, or a shank the collet or bore can't take is refused by name.
- **`SetToolBody::library(world, tool, entry, gauge_len, projection)`** (app). It drops a library entry into a tool's holder as one undoable command, built on `SetToolBody::spun`. The holder lands as a drawn profile and stays editable. The gauge length defaults to the entry's own. The projection (nose face above the tip) defaults to the tool's flute plus shank length. Collision checks judge it through the existing body path (`tool_body::judged` / `stack`), with no new collision code.
- **Tool editor, Profile tab:** a "Holder library" section with a "Library holder" picker, a gauge length field, a one-line dimension summary, a live shank-fit refusal, and "Apply holder" (one undo step). After it lands, the holder edits as a Custom profile.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/793-taper-holders.md` has the dimension table, its sources, and the small-BT decision.

## Dimension table (mm, summary; the sources are in the decision file)

| Taper | Gauge Ø | Flange Ø | Gauge line to flange back | Flange thickness | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BT30 | 31.75 | 46 | 2 | 20 | JIS B 6339 / MAS 403 |
| BT40 | 44.45 | 63 | 2 | 25 | JIS B 6339 / MAS 403 |
| CAT40 | 44.45 | 63.5 | 3.175 | 15.875 | ASME B5.50-2009 Table 1 |

ER nuts (DIN 6499 standard round nut; ISO 15488 collet ranges):

| Size | Nut Ø × length | Collet range Ø |
|---|---|---|
| ER16 | 32 × 17.5 | 0.5-10 |
| ER20 | 35 × 19.5 | 1-13 |
| ER25 | 42 × 20 | 1-16 |
| ER32 | 50 × 22.5 | 2-20 |

Weldon bodies (DIN 1835 B bores, typical DIN 6359 bodies) run from Ø25 for the 6 mm bore to Ø52 for the 20 mm bore.

**BT30 ER20** (the 770MX holder) at its default 60 mm gauge length:
- ER20 nut Ø35 × 19.5;
- body Ø35;
- flange Ø46 × 20, with its front face 22 mm from the gauge line;
- 2 mm standoff to the gauge line.

The flange's gripper groove and drive slots, the nut's chamfers and the body's neck are enveloped, never cut away. The taper inside the spindle is left out, so the spindle housing rides on the gauge line.

**Small BT sizes (BT10/15/20/25):** not included. JIS B 6339 (ISO 7388) and ASME B5.50 start at size 30. No public standard table was found for the small sizes; their makers' dimensions differ. The decision file has the reasoning.

## How tested

- `camcraft-tools` (lib), `holder_library::tests`:
  - `the_tapers_and_nuts_match_the_recorded_table`
  - `the_bt30_er20_outline_is_the_table` (every point of the user's holder)
  - `every_entry_draws_a_valid_profile_with_its_flange_and_nose`
  - `a_longer_gauge_raises_the_flange_and_keeps_the_nose`
  - `nonsense_is_refused_by_name`

title: feat(post,machine): Tormach microARC 4 - A indexing in the PathPilot post
body:
Tormach microARC 4 as an A rotary about X: a new 770MX + microARC 4 machine file, and indexed 4-axis work in the PathPilot post. Simultaneous 4-axis is refused by name and split off to #796. Includes the hardware test kit the user asked for.

Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed
- **Machine file** `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` ("Tormach 770MX + microARC 4", registered in `posting::MACHINES`): the 770MX's figures plus an A rotary part, `axis: [1, 0, 0]`, travel -360..360 degrees. No rates are stated; TD10749 gives none, and absent is never zero.
  - The **direction sense** is the sign of the axis vector: `[1,0,0]` is RS-274 / ISO 841 (a + A turns the tool right-handed about +X relative to the part), and `[-1,0,0]` negates the posted A. This is documented in `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`.
- **Post** `assets/posts/tormach.cps`:
  - A tilted section is indexed at its first motion: `G53 G0 Z<safe>`, then `G0 A..` alone, then the X Y first move.
  - The section's tips are posted in the turned frame: relative to the work offset, turned by -A about X. So **WCS Y0 Z0 must lie on the A centerline**, and the post writes an operator note at the first index.
  - A is read **through the tool axis**, not the letters, so the pose law's canonical A0 B180 (the face underneath) posts as `G0 A180`.
  - A machine with an A writes `G0 A..` at its first motion, `A0` for upright work: a program never assumes where the last run left the table. A machine without one writes no A at all, so every existing golden is byte-identical.
  - No A word ever rides a cutting move, and no clamp code is written.
- **Refused by name:** a tilt the A axis can't reach (any X component in the tool axis, any C); an A past the stated travel; an A that changes inside an operation ("simultaneous 4-axis motion ... not confirmed on PathPilot"); an arc on an indexed A; and a tilt on a machine with no A about X.
- **Parser fix found on the way** (`crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs`): the head search used `get("parts")?`, so it stopped at the first leaf part. Any file with a leaf (like the new A rotary) ahead of its head silently lost its spindle range, belt ranges, rigid tapping and coolant. It now passes leaves over.
- **Test kit** `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/`:
  - The part: 3/4" bar, 1.5" stick-out, G54 X0 at the end face, Y0 Z0 on the A centerline, A0 at a marked line.
  - The cuts: two opposite 0.015" flats at A-90 / A90 (1/4" end mill), and a 0.020" cross groove back at A0 (1/8" end mill).
  - The files: the project built by the app (`microarc_test_part.camproj`), its posted program (`microarc_test_part.nc`, pinned), and a README with the setup, the safety steps (A-direction check by MDI `G0 A90`, collet-nut clearance, air-cut with Z raised and single-block) and a checklist.
  - The continuous op (a Rotary Parallel wrap on the same bar) is refused by name now and is pinned as #796's test.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/785-microarc-4th-axis.md`.

## The three questions (answered on #785)
1. **Wrapped or linear A?** No source settles it. The Tormach guides are silent, and LinuxCNC leaves rollover to each machine's configuration. So: indexing only, and any A that changes inside an operation is refused.
2. **Clamp or brake M-code?** None. The microARC 4 (harmonic drive) has no clamp, and the older tables (TD10552, TD10374) clamp by hand and must be released to rotate. The post writes an operator note instead.
3. **Combined XYZA feed?** Under LinuxCNC G94, F is the XYZ feed and A is carried along; G93 is listed in Tormach's guidelines. Neither is confirmed on the microARC, so nothing combined is posted: A only ever moves alone, with Z up. Split off to #796.

## How tested
- **`crates/app/tests/tormach_fourth_axis.rs`** (new, 10 tests):
  - `the_microarc_machine_states_an_a_about_x`: the machine schema, plus the parser fix.
  - `an_indexed_four_face_job_posts_a_between_operations`: the golden `golden/nc/tormach/index_4face_microarc4.nc`. Each face's posted square equals the hand-rotated local square.
  - `an_upright_job_states_a0_on_the_4th_axis_machine_only`, `a_reversed_a_vector_posts_the_angle_negated`, `the_canonical_b180_pose_posts_as_a180`.
  - The refusals: `a_tilt_the_a_axis_cannot_reach_is_refused`, `an_a_past_travel_is_refused`, `an_a_that_changes_inside_an_operation_is_refused`, `an_arc_on_an_indexed_a_is_refused`, `a_tilt_on_a_machine_with_no_a_about_x_is_refused`.
- **`crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs`** (new):
  - `the_microarc_test_part_posts_its_indexed_program`: the kit is built through the app's commands, passes the verification gate, posts byte-equal to the kit `.nc`, and its project file names its ops.
  - `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_is_refused_by_name`: the gate refuses the wrap op, and the post refuses it as simultaneous 4-axis.
- **Each refusal fails its test when removed.** Five mutants of `tormach.cps`, each with one refusal disabled; each fails exactly its pinning test (9 pass, 1 fail per mutant).
- Ran green locally: conformance (no other post's golden changed), machine, machine_library, machine_edit, tormach_post, tormach_machines, tormach_safe_retract, probe_tormach, tilt, rotary_letter, posting, camcraft-post unit tests, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`.
- Linux quick gate (`--base upstream/main`): green, post suites + app suites, 9.2 min, 0 failed.

## Not exercised
- The PathPilot Hub, and the user's 770MX with a microARC 4. Those runs come later; the kit is ready for them.
- The real direction sense of the microARC 4 on PathPilot: the kit's first step checks it.
- **Known limit (#797):** the app's machine check judges tilt letters with no IK, so A0 B180 (the face at 180 degrees) is refused at the program gate even though the post can write it. The kit uses A-90 / A90 for the opposite pair.
- Other mills with a microARC 4 (1100MX and so on): copy the file and add the rotary part.

Changelog: Tormach PathPilot post indexes a 4th axis (A about X) between operations, with the new Tormach 770MX + microARC 4 machine; simultaneous 4-axis, unreachable tilts and A past travel are refused by name; machine files with a leaf part ahead of the head keep their spindle and coolant figures
