title: feat(sim,app): plasma verification laws block the post (#672 step 2)
body:
Step 2 of the plasma through-cut laws (#672, part of #621), after step 1's `plasma_laws` module (#675). fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

**The program is read from the records, never from text.** `PlasmaProgram::from_toolpath(&Toolpath)` (`crates/sim/src/verify/plasma/program.rs`) builds the laws' input from `Toolpath::plasma` (#676): each `TorchSpan`'s lit moves chorded at 0.01 mm sagitta into the cut path, the torch-off travel between spans as the rapid into each cut, `small` from the span. A path with no record, or one `PlasmaCut::is_sane` rejects, is refused by name - nothing is guessed from bare moves.

**A refusal blocks the post.** `posting::plasma_clause` (`crates/app/src/posting_plasma.rs`) runs inside `verification_report`, beside the stock-sim clause, so every surface that reads the gate - `post_setup`, the per-op and per-mount posts, the script API, the status line - blocks on a plasma refusal: `post blocked - Plasma1: plasma cut order: contour C0 is cut after contour C1, which encloses it - ...`. The 3D stock sim carves nothing for a torch (it skips the op, as before); that skip is now stated on the gate's not-judged line: `stock sim did not judge this program: ... the 3D stock sim does not run for plasma - Plasma1 judged by the 2D plasma laws (cut order, cut crossing, kerf crossing, tip-up): clean` (or the warnings, named, in document units). A plasma op with no path, or a path with no record, is a blocking problem of its own.

**Laws (sim::verify::plasma, now a directory module: `mod.rs` laws, `geom.rs`, `shape.rs` door, `program.rs` reader):**
- **Cut crossing (refusal, new):** a later contour's ring properly crossing an earlier contour's ring - the kerf runs through a part already cut, the through-cut's 2D gouge. The ring is the stretch of a cut between the first point it returns to and that return, so a lead running over an earlier kerf stays the torch-height *warning*.
- **Enclosure recomputed from the rings** (step-1 review): each cut's parent is the smallest ring enclosing every point of its ring (its path for an open run / one-point small hole); a `PARENT` the geometry disagrees with is refused by name, each way round. Cut order runs on the verified parent.
- Step-1 review notes: `small` only on `INNER`; a one-point cut without `small` is "no cut path" (pinned by name); a parent that is an open run is malformed; a closed-role cut whose path never returns to its start is malformed.
- **Tip-up judges the rapid piece by piece** (review fix): the rapid is split at every contact with a freed part's ring (a proper crossing, a corner it passes through, the ends of a stretch along an edge) and any piece whose midpoint lies strictly inside the part is a tip-up - so a rapid in or out through a corner is caught, while one that leaves from the part's own edge outward is not.
- **Cut crossing also refuses rings that meet only at vertices or collinear edges** (review fix): a later ring with a piece strictly inside the earlier ring and a piece strictly outside it runs through the part; two parts sharing an edge (common-line cutting) stay legal.
- `PlasmaFinding` gained `describe()`, `at()` and `Display`.

**The cover law (#676 decision 12), at generation** - `crates/motion/src/plasma/laws.rs` (`kerf_law` moved there from `emit.rs`): an outward offset bridges a slot or notch narrower than the kerf (an inward one drops a keyway narrower than the kerf from a hole) as one loop, so `kerf_ring` accepted it and the feature was silently left in the material. `cover_law` samples every edge of every closed contour at 0.25 mm and refuses by name any point farther than one kerf width (2r + `KERF_TOL`) from its own cut's lit chords: `contour C0: the torch never comes within a kerf of the part edge near X.. Y.. - a slot, notch or inside corner narrower than the kerf (1.500 mm) is bridged by the offset, not cut; widen it or use a narrower kerf`. **Sharp inside corners are not refused** (review note, decided by the main session): every inside corner leaves a kerf-radius tip the torch cannot reach - normal for plasma - so the law exempts each inside corner's tip zone, the stretch of wall r (tan(δ/2) − √3) from the vertex that even the ideal miter path leaves beyond 2r (δ the turn; empty for openings of 60° and more, 1.5 mm at 30°), and judges only the material beyond it. The refusal names the gap it measured: `a slot, notch or keyway about 1.000 mm across, narrower than the kerf (1.500 mm), is bridged by the offset, not cut; widen it past the kerf or use a narrower kerf`. Reasoning and the dropped measures in `docs/decisions/672-plasma-laws-2.md` (items 3 and 4a).

**#674's machine-check note** now names where the through-cut IS judged (the plasma laws at the post gate, the kerf and cover laws at generation; the 3D stock sim does not run for a torch).

## How tested

All run locally (debug), plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean:

- `camcraft-sim` `plasma_laws` 17/17 (step 1's 8 unchanged + 9 new: `a_small_mark_on_anything_but_a_hole_is_refused`, `a_one_point_cut_without_the_small_mark_is_refused`, `an_open_parent_is_malformed`, `a_closed_contour_whose_cut_never_closes_is_refused`, `a_stated_parent_the_rings_disagree_with_is_refused`, `a_ring_crossing_an_earlier_ring_is_refused`, `a_rapid_leaving_a_freed_parts_edge_is_not_a_tip_up`; review fixes: `a_rapid_through_a_freed_parts_corner_is_a_tip_up` - the review's three fixtures (50,25)→(-50,-25), (0,0)→(70,70), (-10,-10)→(70,70) each warn, placed inside the part, and a rapid along the edge stays clear; `an_overlapping_ring_meeting_only_at_vertices_and_edges_is_refused` - `square(0,0,50)` then `square(25,0,50)` refused, the shared-edge pair legal).
- `camcraft-sim` `plasma_program` 5/5 (new): spans -> cuts and rapids; the outline-before-hole program refused from the record (plus the tip-up the pierce inside the freed outline earns); lit arcs chorded; a rapid over a freed part read and warned; no record / record off the moves refused by name.
- `camcraft-motion` `plasma::tests` 13/13 (11 unchanged + `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged`: a 1 mm notch under a 1.5 kerf refused, located and its 1.000 mm gap named against the kerf, the same notch 3 mm wide cuts, a 1 mm keyway on a hole refused; `a_sharp_inside_corner_generates_with_its_tip_left_not_refused`: 30°, 45° and 55° V-notches 20 mm wide generate).
- `camcraft-app` `plasma_gate` 4/4 (new): the generated holed plate is clean and the report says the 3D sim did not run for it (the post on the 1300PL writes, carrying the line); the same cuts re-laid outline-first block `post_setup` with `post blocked - Plasma1: plasma cut order ...`; a generated record with the outline naming the hole as its parent blocks with the disagreement by name; an ungenerated plasma op and a path without its record are named problems.
- `camcraft-app` `plasma_machine` 6/6 (note assertion extended), `plasma_profile` 7/7, `post_not_judged` 4/4 (a milling program still reports no line), `conformance` 6/6, `golden_cl` 24/24.

Each law is pinned by a fixture that trips it and one that passes (see the suites above). Linux batch gate: see the comment below.

## Remove-the-refusal checks

Each refusal was removed in turn (source patched, test run, file restored - the tree is back at the commit) and its pinning test(s) failed; with the refusal back, each passes:

| Refusal removed | Pinning test(s) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| cut order (`judge`) | sim `plasma_laws::an_outline_before_its_hole_is_refused_by_name`; app `plasma_gate::an_outline_cut_before_its_hole_blocks_the_post_by_name` | FAILED, FAILED |
| cut crossing (`judge`) | sim `plasma_laws::a_ring_crossing_an_earlier_ring_is_refused` | FAILED |
| enclosure disagreement (`shape`) | sim `plasma_laws::a_stated_parent_the_rings_disagree_with_is_refused`; app `plasma_gate::a_parent_the_rings_disagree_with_blocks_the_post_by_name` | FAILED, FAILED |
| `small` only on INNER (`shape`) | sim `plasma_laws::a_small_mark_on_anything_but_a_hole_is_refused` | FAILED |
| one-point cut without `small` (`shape`) | sim `plasma_laws::a_one_point_cut_without_the_small_mark_is_refused` | FAILED |
| open-run parent (`shape`) | sim `plasma_laws::an_open_parent_is_malformed` | FAILED |
| closed cut that never closes (`shape`) | sim `plasma_laws::a_closed_contour_whose_cut_never_closes_is_refused` | FAILED |
| cover law call (`emit`) | motion `plasma::tests::a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` | FAILED |
| gate wiring (`problems.extend(plasma.problems)` in `verification_report`) | app `plasma_gate::an_outline_cut_before_its_hole_blocks_the_post_by_name`, `a_plasma_op_with_no_path_is_a_named_problem_not_a_silence`, `a_parent_the_rings_disagree_with_blocks_the_post_by_name` | FAILED, FAILED, FAILED |
| tip-up piece split (`crosses_area` back to endpoint-inside-or-proper-crossing) | sim `plasma_laws::a_rapid_through_a_freed_parts_corner_is_a_tip_up` | FAILED |
| vertex/collinear ring crossing (`rings_cross` back to proper-only) | sim `plasma_laws::an_overlapping_ring_meeting_only_at_vertices_and_edges_is_refused` | FAILED |
| inside-corner tip zone (`tip_zone` returns 0) | motion `plasma::tests::a_sharp_inside_corner_generates_with_its_tip_left_not_refused` (the 30° notch refused again); `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` still passes - the zone is empty at 90° | FAILED |

title: refactor(sim): a carried field bakes the turn's signed permutation into its bricks (#637 E2a)
body:
Stacked on #782 (E1, `issue/637-carried-stock-field`). Until #782 merges, this diff also shows E1's commit. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What changed

#637 step E2a, route (ii) of the [step-E design](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637#issuecomment-6787218007).

- `SdfField::turned(&LatticeTurn) -> (SdfField, Point3)` (new `field_turn.rs`) bakes the turn's signed permutation into the data and returns the translation as the residual view. Brick `b` maps to `!b` (`== -b-1`, total on `i32`, so it can't overflow and there is no failure arm) on a negated axis, with the slot mirrored (`s -> 7 - s`). Axes are swapped on a quarter turn. Band bricks, cuts, `cut_ups` and `cut_downs` are re-indexed and never re-sampled. Shell facets and the closed-form box are negated or swapped exactly.
- New `cut_downs` layer on `SdfField`, the mirror of `cut_ups`. On a flip the two maps trade places: the swap is the record. Nothing reads it yet (E2b).
- A flipped bake that has cuts sets `bounded_cuts`. The E1 monotone floor law assumes cuts came from above, so until E2b's up-march exists, a floor a cut came near is refused by name (`CutFromBelow`).
- Cost ledger: `full` is re-keyed, `region` is rebuilt, and every cut brick is marked dirty (the ledger stays a superset of what moved).
- `LatticeTurn::shift()` (pub) and `linear()` (crate) accessors.
- `field.rs` split by the 400-line law. The input gate (`validate_shell`, `edge_key` and their tests) moved to `field_shell.rs` and is re-exported. `field.rs` goes from 467 to 340 lines.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/779-field-turn-bake.md`.

## How tested

- `field_carry::a_baked_turn_reads_bit_for_bit_what_the_view_reads`: for all 8 turns, on a block field (closed-form box plus a slot) and on a mesh-seeded field (band bricks plus a ball slot), `turned(t).0.distance(p - shift)`, `mesh_distance` and `inside` are bit-identical to `CarriedField::new(f, t)`. The stated scope is points off the lattice planes and off the shell's crossings.
- `carry_engine_agreement::a_baked_turn_reads_what_the_view_reads_through_every_turn`: covers the top slot, the through-slot, the floor sliver and the off-grid ball slot. For all 8 turns, the distance at every column centre of the carried lattice, at each cell-centre height, is bit-identical. For the 4 upright turns, the whole `column_body` read-back (tops, floors, `empty_at`, `floor_judged`) is bit-identical too. A mutation check (slot mirror removed) makes this test fail.
- Unit tests in `field_turn`: four quarter turns restore every layer, the mesh, `region` and `full` bit for bit. A flip moves each `cut_ups` record to the mirrored cell's `cut_downs` and back again, and sets `bounded_cuts`. A bake marks every cut brick dirty, and an upright bake leaves `bounded_cuts` unset.
- Quick gate green (27 sim suites incl. `stock_backend_parity`, `stock_carry`; motion `posed_subtract`; app `stock_export`, `verify`; 2.3 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. The Linux batch gate is running.
- Column-engine verdicts, goldens and snapshots are unchanged. No existing test was edited apart from gate-map header lines.

## Not exercised

- The column read-back of a **flipped** bake. Its floor under a cut needs E2b's `march_up` reading `cut_downs`, and until then it refuses by name. This PR pins only the flipped bake's distance.
- No caller uses `turned` yet. E2c (`CarriedField::simulate`) is the first. The view (`CarriedField`) stays the carried read.

title: refactor(motion): machining3d, multiaxis and quality read stock through Stock/Columns
body:
M7.3 (4/6): camcraft-motion now reads and cuts stock only through the `Stock` / `Columns` seam. It names no `Dexel` outside tests.

## What changed
- **Masks:** `pocket3d_prev`, `pocket3d_with_rest_prev`, `pocket3d_offset_prev`, `pocket3d_offset_with_rest_prev` and `multiaxis_rough_prev` take `Option<&Columns<'_>>` instead of `Option<&Dexel>`. The app (`operation/generate.rs`) wraps its program-ahead grid with `Columns::of_grid`, which borrows and does not clone, as #595 did.
- **Motion's own sims** (`sim_of`, `run_rest`, `optimize_feed`, `quality::{stock_for, measure, rest_area}`) hold a `Stock` on `Backend::Column`.
  - They read through `Columns`: `above` for the rest and mask targets, `top_over` for the feed sampler and the contact rim, `top_at`/`center` for `rest_area`.
  - They score with `Stock::measure`.
  - `optimize_feed` now goes through `engagement_on`; the private `engagement` is gone.
- **New seam ops** in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/backend_edit.rs`:
  - `Stock::subtract_flat`, `Stock::cut_chord` and `Stock::set_tops`. On the column arm each one is the old `Dexel` call, unchanged.
  - On the field arm, the flat tool cuts with the spanning flank. `set_tops` refuses by name (`SET_TOPS_FIELD_REFUSAL`).
  - A posed cutting move is refused on both arms (`POSED_REFUSAL`).
  - `Columns::to_stock` gives the rest pass its owned copy of the mask. This is the same clone `run_rest` already made.
- **`Result` returns:** `quality::measure` and `quality::rest_area` now return `Result`, because a seam cut can refuse. That is test-only API (the yardstick).
- **Decision:** recorded in `docs/decisions/587-motion-onto-stock.md`.

## How tested

title: refactor(sim): a field column's floor under a cut reads exactly by the monotone law
body:
## What changed

**#637 step E1** (fork synced at v0.16.0; branched from upstream/main). The design for step E - the holders' mutation path, the two routes for cutting a carried field, the build order - is on the issue (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637#issuecomment-6787218007); E2a-c are filed as #779, #780, #781 and the holders stay #586's. This PR is the first slice, which stands alone: **a field column's floor under a cut is read exactly**, so `CarriedField::column_body` (step D) carries through-holes, through-slots and floor slivers instead of refusing the whole carry.

- **The monotone law** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_floor.rs`): every tool `Stock::simulate` builds spans the verdict world above its tip (`spanning_flank`), so its swept solid holds every point above any point it holds. A column's material is therefore one interval `[shell floor, tool bottom]` or nothing: a cut from above lowers the top and never raises the floor. New `SdfField::column_span(x, y) -> ColumnSpan { Material { top, floor } | Empty | CutFromBelow | Unreadable }`:
  - the down-march's `Top` proves a material centre, so the floor is the shell's lowest crossing (exact);
  - `NoMaterial` is cut through OR a sliver thinner than a cell with no centre in it; the cut layer's own ray-entry record (`cut_ups`) at the cell below the floor plane gives the tool's bottom (`centre + entry`, closed-form under a flat floor), and material stands iff it is not below the floor - the column body's `top < floor` empty law, same strictness;
  - a record that must exist and does not is refused by name (`Unreadable`), never read as air.
- **A bounded tool suspends the law.** A solid that does not span the world above its tip - the truncated taper (`backend.rs`'s "chimney"), a bare ball, a lathe sweep, a posed axis - sets `bounded_cuts` on the field (`subtract_batch`, past every gate so a refusal leaves the field as it stood; `Sweep::spans_above`, `ArcPiece::spans_above`), and a floor a cut came within a cell of is then refused as step B refused every cut (`CutFromBelow`).
- `floor_at` keeps its API as `column_span`'s floor; `field_body::read_column` reads one `column_span` per column (one march instead of one march plus a floor read).
- **A column reads at its cell centre.** A query a hair inside a cut whose cell centre stands outside reads as its cell does (the field's `distance` / `column_top` law): material over-reported at the lattice's resolution, never air where steel stands. The #649-review test now pins that contract instead of the refusal.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/637-carried-stock-field.md` (route (ii) over (i), the dropped `cut_downs`-at-every-claim, the dropped lattice origin).

title: fix(motion,app): trochoidal slot refuses by name at the loop and helix caps, bounds the microlift
body:
Stacked on #563 (branch `issue/220-trochoidal-slot`); merges after it.

Follow-ups from the high-tier review of #563: each of the three is now a named refusal, never a misleading message or a silent substitute (Prime Directive).

## What changed

1. **Loop-cap refusal names its cause** (`trochoid_slot.rs`). When every rung of the step ladder needs more than the 20000-loop cap, the refusal now reads "the forward step is too small - a 0.0001 mm forward step along the 40.000 mm centre line needs more than the 20000 loop cap ...; raise the forward step". Before, it said "the least, inf deg at (0.000, 0.000), was read at a 0.0001 mm step". When longer rungs were measured over the engagement limit and the shorter ones hit the cap, the engagement refusal stays and adds the cap as the reason no shorter step was tried.
2. **Microlift height bound: the clearance above the cut top.**
   - App: `OpParams::microlift_refusal(clearance, top)` in `operation/types/sane.rs` holds the rule. `operation::microlift_sane` asks it with resolved heights, and `heights_gate` (create, parameter edit, source change) calls that and refuses by name.
   - Motion: `TrochoidParams::validate` refuses the same law as a backstop, so no feed return is posted above the clearance plane.
   - Why the clearance plane and not a stated maximum: see `docs/decisions/774-trochoid-refusals.md`.
3. **Helix-turn cap is a refusal.** `helix_turns(..).unwrap_or(1.0)` is gone. A level whose bore needs more than `MAX_HELIX_TURNS` (1024) turns is refused by name, giving the drop, the helix radius and the fix (a smaller stepdown or a wider loop band). `emit_level` now returns `Result`.
4. Refactor for the 400-line limit: `contained` and `arc_samples` move unchanged from `trochoid_slot.rs` (now 397 lines) to `trochoid_loops.rs` (336 lines).

## How tested

New pinning tests. Each one fails on the #563 head without this change:
- `crates/motion/tests/trochoid_slot.rs`
  - `trochoid_step_past_the_loop_cap_is_refused_by_that_cause`: before, the refusal read "... the least, inf deg at (0.000, 0.000) ...".
  - `trochoid_microlift_above_the_clearance_plane_is_refused`: before, a 100 mm lift returned `Ok`. A lift exactly at the bound is still accepted.
  - `trochoid_bore_past_the_helix_turn_cap_is_refused`: before, a 6200 mm single level returned `Ok`, cutting the whole drop in one helix turn.
- `crates/app/tests/trochoid_op.rs`

Also run, all green:
- full `trochoid_slot` (motion, 10 tests) and `trochoid_op` (app, 5 tests)

title: docs(site): Zola documentation site, deployed to GitHub Pages at each release tag
body:
First cut of #688: the documentation site, built with Zola and published to GitHub Pages from the tag-triggered release workflow. The browser build (`/app/`) waits for #31; the front page says it is coming.

## What changed
- **`site/`** - a Zola project with our own Tera templates (`base`, `index`, `section`, `page`) and one plain stylesheet: no third-party theme, no framework, no JavaScript. Light/dark follows the OS.
  - **User guide** (`content/guide/`): Install, First run, Setups, Operations, Posting, Reading a refusal.
  - **Developers** (`content/developers/`): Crate map, Commands and undo, Test gates (`cargo xtask gate`), Releases.
  - Front page: what CamCraft is, the pre-1.0 caution, the version the site was built from with a download link to that release, and the "browser build is coming (#31)" note.
  - Written from the README, AGENTS.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md, `docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md` and the code (ribbon labels, tab names, `KindInfo::ALL` captions, `posting.rs` refusal messages, the Post refused window). Clean room: only CamCraft's own behaviour; no vendor text, no Fusion output.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** - **needs the maintainer's look** (`.github` change):
  - `site` job (contents: read): installs Zola **v0.23.6** (musl binary from the official release, SHA-256 checked), reads `[workspace.package] version`, refuses a tag that doesn't name it, writes `site/version.toml`, runs `zola build --base-url https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>`, uploads with `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`. On a manual dispatch it only builds.
  - `pages` job: `actions/deploy-pages@v5`, `pages: write` + `id-token: write` scoped to this job only, `github-pages` environment, `pages` concurrency group. Runs only on a tag, when `site` and `publish` both succeeded, so the site's download link never points at a missing release.
  - **No new trigger**; the workflow default stays `contents: read`.
- `.gitignore`: `site/public/`, `site/version.toml`. Nothing generated is committed.
- `docs/decisions/688-docs-site.md`: the choices and what was dropped.

## Repo settings the deploy needs (cannot be set from a workflow)
- Settings > Pages > Source: **GitHub Actions**.
- Environment `github-pages` > deployment branches and tags: allow tags `v*.*.0` (the default allows protected branches only and would refuse a tag deploy).

## How tested
Zola 0.23.6 (official aarch64-apple-darwin binary, checksum-verified, in a temp dir):
- `zola build` -> `Creating 10 pages (0 orphan) and 2 sections`, no warnings.
- `zola check` -> `Site content: 10 pages (0 orphan), 2 sections`, every internal and external link OK (one GitHub `#anchor` link that Zola can't resolve was dropped).
- With `version.toml` = 0.16.0 and `--base-url https://mkinney.github.io/Camcraft`: front page reads "This site documents CamCraft 0.16.0" with a link to `releases/tag/v0.16.0`, footer "Built from CamCraft 0.16.0", all asset and page links carry the base path; without the file it says it's a local preview.
- The workflow's version `sed` run locally against `Cargo.toml` -> `0.16.0`; the musl tarball's checksum and layout (`zola` at the root) checked; the YAML parses (jobs: ..., publish, site, pages).
- No Rust changed, so no cargo gate applies.

## Not exercised
- The Pages deploy itself: it runs only on a pushed `vX.Y.0` tag. The `site` job's Linux steps ran only as their local equivalents above.
- Actions minutes: the first tag run's added minutes get measured and reported on #688 afterwards (the `site` job is a ~10 MB download plus a sub-second build; `pages` is a deploy).
- AGENTS.md's release steps don't name the site step yet: that's a process-file change (PROCESS_VERSION bump, #681 note), left for a process PR once the job has run once.

title: feat(app,ui): set the WCS from any set of feature picks (#701)
body:
You can select edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls and say which axis each one sets (#701) - the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable like any other placement.

## The change

**App lane** - `pick::roles.rs`: `Role` (`Origin | X | Y | Z`) and `align_roles(world, picks) -> Result<Alignment, String>`, returning the same `Alignment` `pick::align`'s 3-2-1 fit already returns, so one fit law answers both. Frame law: among the axis picks present, read in the priority order Z, X, Y - first exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the right-handed frame (a third axis pick is overridden wholesale, not blended). An origin pick anchors on the feature's natural centre; without one the origin stays the model's own. Refusals come back as words, in order: too few picks, a duplicated role, fewer than two axes, an unresolvable datum, an unsupportable tilt, a stale feature id. Cylinder walls fit by covariance null-space (Jacobi) plus a Kasa circle, on the wall's local facets transformed by the feature's `setup_align::view_pose` - the same law the plane fit already uses.

**UI lane** - the Setups page grows a "Set WCS from features" row (`egui_app::wcs_pick_row.rs`) over a draft module (`wcs_pick.rs`): arming it keeps the toolbar's pick mode (faces, edges, corners and walls all feed the one draft), the role box says what the next pick sets, and each viewport pick is stamped into that role's slot - re-picking a role replaces its pick in place. One draft at a time: arming this row disarms the plane-pick and axis-pick drafts and vice versa, and the wcs draft pauses while its setup row is hidden (the #664 law). Apply is gated live by `align_roles` itself - the refusal words ride the row inline and on the disabled button, so the UI's why is the command's own words - and queues the existing undoable `CommandKind::SetWcs`; the same command the WCS pane's anchor grid already sends. No new command kind, no world writes outside commands. Rationale in `docs/decisions/701-wcs-from-features.md`.

## Pins (red before the fix, green with it)

- `wcs_roles::z_face_x_edge_and_origin_corner_reproduce_the_3_2_1_frame` - a Z face, X edge and origin corner digit-for-digit reproduce `align_321`.
- `wcs_roles::the_third_axis_role_is_derived_right_handed_never_read` - three axis picks: the third is overridden wholesale and the frame is right-handed.
- `wcs_roles::the_origin_projects_onto_a_z_face_and_anchors_on_its_centroid` - an origin vertex pick anchors on the face's centroid, projected onto its plane.
- `wcs_roles::a_tilted_bore_wall_fits_its_real_axis_and_centre` / `a_bore_wall_picked_as_z_stands_upright_with_a_pinned_sign` - the wall fit, both flat and tilted, sign pinned by the axis role.
- `wcs_roles::every_degenerate_role_set_is_refused_by_name` - each refusal sentence, pinned.
- `egui_app::wcs_pick_tests::*` - four kittest tests on the live row: arming keeps the pick mode and stops the other drafts; an incomplete set greys Apply and shows the app's own words; role picks land in the draft (never in the open operation) and Apply queues one undoable `SetWcs` that undo/redo round-trips; re-picking replaces only that role's pick.
- `wcs_pick::tests::*` - three draft-module tests: role default and mutual disarm, replace-in-place, a paused draft takes nothing.

## Tested

title: feat(post): a PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL
body:
**Stacked on #676** (#670, plasma profile), which is stacked on #674 (#669, plasma kind). Review only this PR's own commit, `2645a023`.

A **PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL** (#671). Every word below was checked against UM10720 v1223A ([UM]) or Tormach's PathPilot Post Processor Guidelines, Plasma column ([PG]).

| Word | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `G20`/`G21` | units | [PG] |
| `G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80` | modal reset, once | [PG]; [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` | path blending (P in inches even under G21) | [UM] §6.2.1 p.50; [PG] |
| `G54` | work offset | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `G43 H1` | torch length offset | [PG] ("always H1"); [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G30` | go to the G30 height | [UM] §6.2.1-6.2.2 |
| `G0 X Y` | rapid to the pierce point, never Z | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `M200` | AutoFS (feed, THC volts, pierce height and delay, amps) | [UM] §6.3 p.51, §7.2 p.54 |
| `M207`/`M208`/`M209 P` | pierce height / cut height / pierce delay, only when the op states them | [UM] §6.3.1 p.52, §7.2 |
| `G15` | ohmic probe; WCS Z = 0 | [UM] §7.1 p.54 |
| `G16` | rise to pierce height, fire, delay, go to cut height, THC on | [UM] §7.1; [PG] |
| `G1/G2/G3 X Y [I J] [F]` | the cut, XY only | [PG] |
| `G41.1`/`G42.1 D<kerf>` … `G40` | control compensation, each on its own line before a straight lead | [PG] |
| `M205` | torch off, Z to the G30 height | [UM] §7.2 |
| `M30` | end | [PG] |

- **Never written:** S, M3-M9, M6, G95-G99, canned cycles.
- **M6 conflict:** [PG] says M6 is unsupported on plasma, but [UM]'s test program writes `T1 M6`. This follows the issue and [PG]; the conflict is recorded.

## What changed
- **Script:** `assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Plasma", the only `PLASMA_POSTS` entry. Milling posts decline a plasma stream, because they lack the torch hooks.
- **Stream:** #676's records are carried into the post stream: `PLASMA …`, `TORCH ON C<id> …` and `TORCH OFF C<id>` (the `.cl` v5 records without `; `).
  - The parser reads both spellings; malformed records are refused by line number.
  - New properties: `PlasmaKerf`, `PlasmaCompensation`, `PierceHeight`, `CutHeight`, `PierceDelay` (absent = AutoFS), `PlasmaFeed`, `PlasmaReversed`, `Contour`, `ContourRole`, `ParentContour`, `SmallHole`.
  - New hooks: `onPlasma`, `onTorchOn`, `onTorchOff`.
  - `machine.kind` is now a script property.
- **Engine torch law** (`cnc_torch.rs`), refused by name:
  - a TORCH with no header, a second header;
  - ON while lit, a wrong or extra OFF, a rapid while lit;
  - a section or stream left lit;
  - a script without both torch hooks.
- **Post refusals:**
  - a non-plasma op, a Plasma Profile path with no plasma record;
  - rpm, coolant (other than off), a rotary or tilted move;
  - Z on a lit move, a canned cycle, a dark feed;
  - comp under a computer offset, wear comp;
  - a machine that isn't `kind: plasma`.
- **AutoFS:** under AUTOFEED, no F is written. A small hole then runs at the AutoFS feed, with an operator comment; refusing it would block every default plate with a hole.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/671-plasma-post.md` (the sources and ten choices). CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md are updated.

## Golden (`tormach-plasma/plasma_plate_with_holes.nc`, inch; excerpt)
```
G20
G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80
G64 P0.005 Q0.005
(T1 PLASMA TORCH - KERF 0.0591)
G54
G43 H1
G30
(C0 INNER IN C4 - SMALL HOLE 65% FEED)
G0 X3.3465 Y0.7874
M200
M207 P0.1496
M209 P0.5
G15
G16
G1 X3.3465 Y0.9547 F63.98
...
M205
G30
```
Siblings: `_mm.nc` and `_control.nc` (`G41.1 D0.0591` … `G40`). The CLI post is byte-identical to the inch golden.

## How tested
- **`plasma_post` (5):**
  - the inch and mm goldens, with structural checks: no Z/S/T/M3-M9/M6, per-contour order, G30 after every M205, ending `G30 M30`;
  - the in-app dump equals the `.cl` golden;
  - the control-comp golden;
  - a stream round-trip, plus malformed-record refusals;
  - an in-app 1300PL document posts through the gate.
- **`plasma_post_refusals` (5):** every refusal, the engine torch law, every milling builtin declining the stream, and the registry.
- **Pins updated:** plasma_machine, machine_library, plasma_profile, golden_cl and conformance.
- **Gate:**
  - those suites plus posting, camcraft-post and camcraft-cl;
  - also tormach_post, control_comp, coolant, after_op, program_comments, fanuc_post, lathe_post, per_op_files and probe_guard;
  - clippy is clean.

## Not exercised (why this is a draft): a PathPilot Hub 1300PL simulator run
It should check:
1. G20 and G21 both load and run, and `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` reads as inches under G21.
2. `G43 H1` without `T1 M6` is accepted.
3. Whether a bare `G30` after `M205` also travels XY (a time cost only).
4. `M207`/`M209` after `M200` override AutoFS.
5. G1 moves with no F take the AutoFS feed.
6. `G41.1 D…` on its own line, a straight lead, then `G40`, with the offset on the right side.
7. G2/G3 under G91.1.
8. Probe and pierce at each G0 point, THC on, M205, and the part matches.

Changelog: A PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL: M200 AutoFS, G15 probe, G16 pierce, M205 torch off, G30; G41.1/G42.1 D<kerf> under control compensation; non-plasma work refused by name (#671)

Fixes #671

title: feat(post): Doosan DNM + Fanuc post processor (#614)
body:
(fork synced at v0.16.0)

Implements a dedicated post-processor dialect for Doosan DNM vertical machining centers with Fanuc 0i / 31i-M controls (#614).

## What changed

- **`assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`**:
  - Clean-room implementation specced from published Fanuc 0i-MODEL F operator programming manuals, Renishaw MP700 / Inspection Plus manuals, DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0`, and real Doosan DNM machine sample program from Issue #614.
  - **High-Speed Smoothing / AICC (`G5.1 Q1 Rx` / `G5.1 Q0`):** Modal Fanuc AI Contour Control lookahead smoothing with machining condition selection (levels `R1` to `R10`, default `R5` matching the real Doosan DNM sample program). Automatically deactivated (`G5.1 Q0`) prior to canned drilling cycles (`G73`, `G81-G89`), probing, tool change, and program close. Out-of-range smoothing levels are strictly refused by name.
    * *Citation:* FANUC Series 0i-MODEL F Operator's Manual (B-64604EN-2/01) §3.3 (p. 19/33, p. 20/34), §3.3.2 (p. 22/36), §14.1 (p. 377–386). Requires Fanuc AICC I (A02B-0340-S603) or AICC II (A02B-0340-S605).
  - **Renishaw Inspection Plus Probing (`G65 P9832` / `G65 P9833`):** Emits `G65 P9832` (probe optical turn-on) on its own block before protected positioning moves (`G65 P9810`) and surface measurement (`G65 P9811`), and emits `G65 P9833` (probe optical turn-off / sleep) on its own block at the end of the probing sequence before spindle stop/retract. Unknown probing styles are strictly refused by name.
    * *Citation:* Renishaw MP700 Probe System Installation and User's Guide (H-2000-5142-02-A) Chapter 4 (p. 4-2 to 4-17) and Chapter 5.
  - **Rotary Table Brake (4th-axis A on separate blocks, no name sniffing):** Emits `M11` (unclamp) on its own separate block before rotary positioning, and `M10` (clamp) on its own separate block after positioning before cutting (never inline with motion blocks). Continuous 4th-axis contouring unclamps before motion and restores clamping at section end. Strict refusal by name if undeclared via options/properties (`rotaryClamp`/`rotaryUnclamp` or `rotaryBrake`) or machine definition.
    * *Citation:* DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0` Part 5 §3 (p. 180) and Part 8 §3 (p. 232) Alarm 2323.
  - **Chip Conveyor Codes & Strict Refusal:** Requires codes to be declared via post options (`chipConveyorStart` / `chipConveyorStop`), properties, or machine definition, and strictly refuses undeclared codes by name.
    * *Citation:* DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0` Part 5 §3 (p. 180) and Part 5 §2.13 (p. 137).
  - **Through-Spindle Coolant (TSC) & Strict Refusal:** Emits Doosan high-pressure TSC M-code `M88` (with `M89`/`M09` on shut-off) when declared in the machine coolants table, or `M8` when `useM8ForTSC` is enabled. Strictly refuses undeclared through-tool coolant by name if the machine lacks a through-tool entry.
    * *Citation:* DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0` Part 5 §3 (p. 180) and Part 6 §2.6 (p. 217).
  - **Manifest cleanup:** Removed unverified `axisInversion` and `probeAxisInversion` manifest flags pending mirrored-stream equivalence test goldens.
- **`docs/evidence/614-dnm5700-sample.nc`**:
  - In-tree real-world sample G-code program provided by community user `@spikeypineapple` on Issue #614 comment 6764944619 confirming real-world DNM 5700 syntax for `G5.1 Q1 R5`, `M07`, and Renishaw Inspection Plus macros.
- **`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch`**:
  - Registered in `posting::MACHINES` and `crates/app/tests/machine.rs` as `"Doosan DNM 5700"` (Kind: Mill).
  - Updated with official DN Solutions DNM 4500/5700/6700 Specification Catalog numbers (X/Y/Z: 1020/570/510 mm, rapids: 36/36/30 m/min, cutting feed: 15 m/min, spindle: 40-12000 RPM, 18.5 kW, rigid tapping, 30-tool ATC, coolants M8/M7/M88, 4th-axis rotary table A).
- **Decision Record**:
  - Recorded in `docs/decisions/614-doosan-dnm-post.md` with all manual citations, page numbers, and design choices.

## How tested

- **`crates/app/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs`** (7/7 passing):
  - `doosan_dnm_posts_basic_milling_clean`: basic program structure, preamble, tool change, work offset, retracts, safe end.
  - `doosan_dnm_through_spindle_coolant_modes`: verifies M88/M89 default TSC and M8 option.
  - `doosan_dnm_rotary_brake_clamp_unclamp`: verifies separate block emission (`M11`, motion block, `M10`) around A-axis moves with `rotaryBrake: true`.
  - `doosan_dnm_high_speed_smoothing_aicc`: verifies `G5.1 Q1 R5` engagement, `G5.1 Q0` deactivation before canned drilling cycles, and custom level `G5.1 Q1 R8`.
  - `doosan_dnm_chip_conveyor`: verifies M31 start and M33 stop with explicit configuration.
  - `doosan_dnm_probing_modes`: verifies `G65 P9832` (probe on) before moves and `G65 P9833` (probe off) at end.
  - `doosan_dnm_refuses_undeclared_codes_by_name`: verifies strict refusal by name for undeclared TSC, undeclared rotary clamp (tested on both generic VMC and DNM machine to ensure no name sniffing), unknown probing style, unbounded smoothing level, and undeclared chip conveyor codes.
- **`crates/app/tests/machine_library.rs`** (11/11 passing):
  - `every_machine_file_in_assets_is_in_the_library`: verifies Doosan DNM 5700 machine is mounted and registered.
- **`crates/app/tests/machine.rs`** (33/33 passing):
  - `every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration`: pinned Doosan DNM 5700.
- **`crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`** (6/6 passing):
  - `every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` across all goldens.
  - `every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles`, `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension`, `the_dialects_actually_differ`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` is completely clean.

Changelog: Doosan DNM post processor aligned with real machine sample program and manual citations (G5.1 Q1 R<n> smoothing, Inspection Plus G65 P9832/P9833 probe on/off, separate block M10/M11 rotary clamp, and strict refusal of undeclared codes) (#614)

Fixes #614

title: docs: first-part example project + auto-rendered tutorial images (#291)
body:
﻿Answers the docs lane of #291 with two pieces, per the plan discussed there.

**`examples/`** - a complete `first-part.camproj` the guide can teach on: our own clean-room flange fixture (model embedded as facets, so the file is self-contained), stock, Face / 2D Pocket / Drill with generated toolpaths, and the posted `first-part.nc`. Built end-to-end through the MCP server; verify is clean; it round-trips through File > Open.

**`docs/images/first-part-*.png`** - four tutorial step pictures that are golden files, not hand-captured screenshots. The docs test in `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render.rs` opens the project through the real open command, steps through `operation_order`, and renders each step with the real viewport pipelines and the real toolpath display (`interact::toolpath_lines`). A normal run compares and fails on drift; `UPDATE_DOCS_IMAGES=1` regenerates - same workflow as the kittest snapshots.

Notes:
- The test lives in the existing `gpu_render` binary on purpose: it shares that binary's GPU lock and adds no new test process (a fifth process racing fallback-device creation across processes is what makes full-suite runs flake).
- While in there, the binary now renders every frame on one shared `OnceLock` device instead of one per frame - the per-frame create/teardown churn was the flake hazard; readbacks are identical and the binary got ~3.5x faster.
- `interact::toolpath_lines`: `pub(crate)` -> `pub` so the test draws through the app's own path display.

Test stability: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test gpu_render` is 10/10 across repeated runs and deterministic through a regen/compare round-trip. The full-suite wgpu flake is pre-existing on `main` (untouched baseline crashed 3 of 4 runs on this machine) and unrelated to this change.

Keeping this draft until the open questions in #291 are answered - images can move to `docs/guide/src/images/` when the mdbook scaffold lands.
